## Goal (as stated by producer)

"Pi in this repo seems to still have the old restart plugin, remove it."

## Seed context

- Type: unset (likely `chore`), priority medium, created 2026-07-31, stage `intake_complete`.
- No description, acceptance criteria, or referenced artifacts were supplied with the title.

## Investigation (plan session, 2026-10-30)

Searched the repository, the Pi agent directory and the Herdr plugin registry for a
restart-related plugin. Findings:

| Location | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| `pi list` (repo cwd) | `No packages installed` |
| `~/.pi/settings.json` | `"packages": []` |
| `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` | no `packages` key (the pre-removal backup `settings.json.bak` still lists `https://github.com/monotykamary/pi-retry`) |
| `~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/monotykamary/pi-retry` | **stale clone still on disk** — `pi-retry` is the extension that retried/restarted the agent loop after errors; its behaviour was absorbed into the Worklog Pi extension's recovery module (WL-0MR269PDV0014ES3, completed) and undeclared from Pi settings |
| repo `.pi/extensions/` | does not exist (no project-level Pi extensions) |
| `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` | `herdr-agent-state.ts`, `proxy-compaction-bridge`, `proxy-sse-signals`, `voice-input`, `worklog` (none restart-related) |
| repo `.worklog/plugins/` (`wl plugins list`) | only `stats-plugin.mjs` — a legacy demo/example Worklog plugin, tracked in git, not restart-related |
| `~/.config/herdr/plugins.json` | `herdr-notes`, `persiyanov.reviewr`, `worklog-selection-list` (none restart-related) |
| repo-wide grep for "restart plugin"; git history for restart-named files | nothing |

**Conclusion:** no artifact in this repository is named — or behaves as — a "restart
plugin", other than `pi-retry`, which is already undeclared from every Pi settings file
(`pi list` reports nothing installed) and survives only as a stale package-cache clone
under `~/.pi/agent/git/`. The remaining candidate in-repo artifact is the legacy
`.worklog/plugins/stats-plugin.mjs`.

## Status: blocked pending producer clarification

The plan cannot be decomposed until the target artifact is identified. Open questions are
recorded in the work-item comment "Planning paused — producer clarification needed" and
the item is flagged `needsProducerReview`. Stage remains `intake_complete`.

# Heartbeat: Surface Audit Progress and Completion Notifications

**Headline:** When the heartbeat dispatches a background audit it is currently invisible — no start signal, no verdict, and silent failure on timeout. This item adds fire-and-forget toasts around the audit invocation plus a durable comment when the audit fails, while keeping heartbeat non-blocking and suppressible for unattended runs.

## Problem statement

The heartbeat skill dispatches audits headlessly (`pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`) whenever the completed/in_review queue reaches 10+ items. From the producer's perspective this work is invisible: there is no live view, no progress signal, and no notification when the audit lands or when it dies (timeout / non-zero exit). The evaluation in [WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7] identified this as the main visibility gap of headless Pi usage.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want to know when a background heartbeat audit starts, is running, and finishes (with its verdict), without polling the worklog.
- **Operators of unattended environments** (cron, CI, schedulers) — must be able to suppress notifications entirely.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when the heartbeat starts an audit, I want a notification so I know background work is happening."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit completes, I want the verdict (`Ready to close: Yes/No`) surfaced so I don't discover it by chance."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit fails or times out, I want the reason surfaced and recorded, because right now nothing at all is left behind."
- "As an operator running heartbeat from cron, I want to turn notifications off so logs aren't spammed."

## Existing state

- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — runtime copy (Pi resolves the project-local `.pi/skills/` path). Full queue branch selects the first non-ready item by `sortIndex` and runs the audit via `subprocess.run([...], timeout=600)`, discarding stdout; on non-zero exit it returns `"Audit failed for <title> (<id>): <stderr>"`, on `TimeoutExpired` it returns `"Audit timed out for ..."`. No notification of any kind.
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — a **second, separately git-tracked copy** (not a symlink) that has drifted: it dispatches `audit_runner.py` instead of `pi -p`. `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` imports this copy and pins the `.pi` copy's sparse-queue behaviour via `TestPiSkillCopyParity`.
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — document behaviour, inputs, exit codes; no notification contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` — the established toast plumbing for TS: fire-and-forget `herdr notification show`, default `bottom-right`, tolerant of ENOENT / non-zero exit / `shown: false` / rate-limited `busy`. Requires `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271` — audit verdicts duplicated into work-item comments are deprecated; the `audit_results` record is the sole consumer of the verdict.

## Desired change

Emit fire-and-forget lifecycle notifications around the audit invocation:

1. **Start** — before spawning the audit subprocess: toast naming the item being audited.
2. **Completion** — after the audit returns: toast with the verdict, derived by re-reading the audit record (`get_audit_result` + `is_ready_to_close`) rather than parsing subprocess stdout.
3. **Failure / timeout** — toast with the reason **and** a durable `wl comment` on the audited item (the reason is recorded nowhere else today). No verdict comment on success, per `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271`.

Suppression: `--no-notify` CLI flag **and** `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY=1` env var, plus a silent no-op whenever the `herdr` binary is unavailable or the toast call fails.

Out of scope / unchanged: the sparse-queue branch (flagging the next item with `--needs-producer-review true`), the `sortIndex` selection rule, and the existing stdout message strings — stdout output is retained so the Pi TUI still shows the outcome when the blocking call returns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Dispatching an audit emits a **start** notification naming the audited work item, emitted before the audit subprocess is spawned (unit-tested).
2. A completed audit emits a **completion** notification containing the verdict derived from the audit record (`Ready to close: Yes` / `No`), not from subprocess stdout (unit-tested).
3. An audit that fails (non-zero exit) or times out emits a notification naming the reason **and** adds a `wl comment` recording the failure reason on the audited item; no comment is written on success (unit-tested).
4. Notification delivery is non-blocking and failure-tolerant: a missing `herdr` binary, non-zero exit, or `busy` response never raises and never changes the script's exit code; notifications are suppressed when `--no-notify` is passed or `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY=1` is set (unit-tested).
5. Tests: existing heartbeat unit and integration tests still pass, and new tests cover the start / completion / failure / suppression paths; `TestPiSkillCopyParity` is extended so both copies are asserted to share the notification behaviour.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` (behaviour, `--no-notify`, `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY`, notification semantics and the herdr `ui.toast.delivery` prerequisite).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Python standard library only — no new dependencies.
- Fire-and-forget delivery: `subprocess.Popen(..., stdio=DEVNULL)` (or equivalent), never blocking the heartbeat, never raising.
- The audit verdict stays authoritative in the `audit_results` record; do not write verdict comments on success (`docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271`).
- Preserve the existing exit-code contract: `0` for normal operation including audit failure/timeout messaging, `1` only for `Heartbeat error` (wl command / JSON parse failures).
- Both copies of `heartbeat.py` must stay in parity; the change lands in both.
- Do not build a general notification framework or a Pi-extension live-progress channel here (see Risks: scope-creep).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — Runtime copy. Add notification helpers (fire-and-forget `herdr notification show`, env/flag suppression), emit start/completion/failure notifications around the `pi -p` audit invocation, add `--no-notify`.
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — Canonical/tested copy. Mirror the same notification behaviour and flag so the two copies stay in parity.
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — Document the notification lifecycle, `--no-notify`, `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY`, and the herdr `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` prerequisite.
- `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — Mirror of the same documentation.
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` — New unit tests for start/completion/failure/suppression; extend `TestPiSkillCopyParity` to cover notifications across both copies.
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat_integration.py` — Confirm the notification path does not break real `wl` interactions (herdr absent → silent no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` — Reference only (TS equivalent of the Python fire-and-forget helper; no change expected).

## Related work

- `Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7)` — completed; motivated this item ("Heartbeat audit progress + completion notification ... instead of silent background runs").
- `Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)` — completed; origin of `heartbeat.py`.
- `Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (WL-0MSACL482002RNYH)` — completed; established `herdr notification show` + `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` as the toast plumbing.
- `Use centered toast for shortcut feedback instead of status line (WL-0MS7EP7U8008DCXO)` — completed; prior art on toast delivery/rate-limit tolerance.

### Related work (automated find-related report)

**Related work items**
- **WL-0MLG60MK60WDEEGE** — Audit comment improvements (completed)
- **WL-0MVAPF0AD006WHE4** — Complete CLI/API surface: `wl reviewed`, filters, api, completion (completed)
- **WL-0MSACL482002RNYH** — Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (completed)

**Repository file matches**
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — toast/notification semantics, `ui.toast.delivery` prerequisite
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — audit dispatch and queue-threshold context
- `CLI.md` — `wl comment` / `wl update` surface used by the notification path

## Risks & assumptions

- **Copy drift (real risk, discovered during intake)** — `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` is a git-tracked duplicate rather than a symlink, and the two copies already dispatch audits differently. Mitigation: implement in both, extend `TestPiSkillCopyParity`; retiring/symlinking the duplicate is a separate candidate item and is **out of scope** here.
- **Toasts can be missed** — herdr rate-limits with `busy` and delivery depends on `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"`; mitigated by keeping human-readable stdout lines and by the durable failure comment.
- **Verdict freshness** — the completion notification re-reads the audit record after the run. Assumption: a crash before writing the record yields no verdict, which is treated as the failure path (notification + comment).
- **Scope creep** — a Pi-extension-based live progress channel (streaming `pi --mode json` events into the TUI) would be a larger change and is deliberately excluded; record it as a linked item if it becomes desirable.
- **Assumption** — producers watch agent work through herdr, so herdr toasts are the appropriate surface; Pi TUI live notifications are not achievable for a script invoked from a blocking `bash` tool call (`ctx.ui.notify()` is extension-only).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which heartbeat copy is in scope?** (a) implement in `skill/heartbeat` canonical + mirror into `.pi/skills/heartbeat`, extending the parity test; (b) only `.pi/skills/heartbeat`; (c) only `skill/heartbeat`. **Recommended:** (a).
  **Answer (operator):** "A (.pi is not a duplicate, it's a symlink, right?)". **Correction/evidence:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` is *not* a symlink — it is a separate git-tracked copy (`git ls-files .pi/skills` → `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`; distinct inode 6427255 vs 6298862) that has drifted to a different audit dispatch. Option (a) is therefore implemented as *change both copies, keep them in parity*, and the duplicate is flagged as a candidate follow-up rather than a no-op. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- **Q2: Where does the verdict/failure surface?** (a) toast only; (b) toasts for all three events + durable `wl comment` only on failure/timeout; (c) toast + full verdict comment every completion. **Recommended:** (b).
  **Answer (operator):** "Can't we have it in the Pi TUI with a comment on failure/timeout? if not then b". **Research:** `ctx.ui.notify()` is an extension-only API (`docs/extensions.md`, `docs/tui.md`); heartbeat invokes the audit from a blocking `bash` tool call with a 600 s timeout, so nothing can render in the Pi TUI before the call returns, and there is no external notify API for scripts (`docs/cli-integration.md`: print/JSON/RPC modes only). Live Pi-TUI progress would require streaming `pi --mode json` events via an extension — a larger, separate change. Outcome: **(b) adopted** (toasts for start/completion/failure + `wl comment` on failure/timeout only), with the existing stdout lines retained so the Pi TUI still shows the result when the call returns. Source: interactive reply + Pi docs research.
- **Q3: How do unattended environments suppress notifications?** (a) `--no-notify` flag + silent no-op when `herdr` is unavailable; (b) env var only; (c) both flag and env var + silent no-op. **Recommended:** (a).
  **Answer (operator):** "c". Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Heartbeat: surface audit progress and completion notifications

# Herdr selection list: shortcut hint bar empty until a chord key is pressed

## Problem statement

In the Herdr "Worklog Selection List" pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), the footer hint bar that shows the available shortcut commands (e.g. `c:create new  i:implement  u:update...  x:close...`) is empty when the list opens. The hints only appear after the user presses the first key of a chord (e.g. `u`), at which point a `chord: u _ ...` footer renders. The behavior is inconsistent: the initial hints are gated behind the `showHelpText` plugin setting, but the chord-in-progress footer is not gated by it.

## Users

Herdr users who run the Worklog Selection List pane and rely on the footer hint bar to discover keyboard shortcuts.

- As a user opening the Worklog Selection List, I want to see the available shortcut commands in the hint bar immediately, so I know which keys are available without pressing them first.
- As a user who has deliberately disabled help text, I want the setting to behave consistently (all hint lines hidden, including chord-mode hints), matching the pi browse widget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `showHelpText` on (the default), the footer hint bar shows the available shortcut commands as soon as the selection list opens — before any chord key is pressed. (No change to the current on-state rendering.)
2. With `showHelpText` off, the chord-in-progress footer (`chord: <keys> _ <hints>`) is also hidden, so no shortcut hints render in any mode — consistent with the pi browse widget's `showHelpText` handling.
3. The `showHelpText` default remains `true` in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (`defaultSettings`), `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options; verify no code path silently defaults it to `false`.
4. The user's local Herdr config (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is set so `showHelpText` is `true` (or the key is removed to fall back to the default), restoring the visible hint bar for the reporter.
5. Automated tests cover: (a) chord-mode footer suppressed when `showHelpText` is `false`, and (b) chord-mode footer present when `showHelpText` is `true`/unset. Full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation is updated to reflect the change: the Herdr README's `showHelpText` description (`packages/herdr/README.md`) accurately states that `false` hides all shortcut hint lines, including chord-mode hints; code comments on the renderer footer and call site explain the gating.

## Constraints

- Keep the `showHelpText` setting; do not remove or repurpose it (operator decision C).
- The Herdr plugin reads settings from `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` (via `loadSettings()`); the repo must not depend on the reporter's local config for tests.
- The chord key *handling* (state machine) must keep working even when the hint footer is hidden — only rendering is affected.
- Backward compatibility for `createListRenderer` callers: adding a renderer parameter must not break existing tests that call it positionally.

## Existing state

- The initial shortcut hints are computed as `dynamicHints` in `runWorklistTui` and passed to the renderer only when `opts.getShowHelpText()` is true (`worklist.ts` ~line 2666: `opts.getShowHelpText() ? dynamicHints : undefined`).
- The renderer footer (`createListRenderer`, `worklist.ts` ~lines 1683–1697) has two branches:
  - chord active (`chordState.pendingKeys.length > 0`): always renders `chord: <keys> _ <hints>` using `chordState.hints` — **not** gated by `showHelpText`.
  - otherwise: renders `[esc] back` nav hint plus `chordHelpHints` — gated by `showHelpText` at the call site.
- With the reporter's config `showHelpText: false` this yields: empty footer on open; `chord: u _ update...` footer once a chord key is pressed — exactly the reported behavior.
- The pi browse widget (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) gates the entire help line (including chord hints `🔗 …`) behind `currentSettings.showHelpText` — consistent, and the reference behavior for this fix.
- The reporter's local config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` currently contains `"showHelpText": false`.

## Desired change

1. Gate the chord-in-progress footer in the renderer behind `showHelpText` so `showHelpText: false` hides all hint lines (normal and chord-mode), matching the pi widget.
   - Suggested approach: add a trailing `showHelpText` parameter to `createListRenderer`'s returned renderer (defaulting to `true` when `undefined`, preserving existing positional callers/tests), render the chord footer only when `isChordActive && showHelpText`, and pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` from `runWorklistTui`'s call site.
2. Add/extend renderer tests covering the chord-footer gating above (see AC 5).
3. Update the reporter's local `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` so `showHelpText` is `true` (or remove the key), restoring the visible hint bar.

## Risks & assumptions

- The chosen behavior (C) means users with `showHelpText: false` get **no** visual chord feedback at all (not even `chord: u _`). This matches the pi widget but is a UX tradeoff — documented in the README update (AC 6).
- Chord key *handling* must keep working with the footer hidden; the fix must only affect rendering. Guard with a test that chord state still accumulates while `showHelpText` is `false`.
- Adding a trailing `showHelpText` param to `createListRenderer` must not break existing positional callers/tests (default `true` when `undefined`).
- The reporter's local config fix (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is out-of-repo; the implementing agent cannot commit it — it must be applied locally (AC 4) or the key removed to use the default.
- Scope-creep guard: adjacent renderer/footer improvements (e.g., "items below the fold" — WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ) are separate work items; do not expand scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` footer branch: gate chord-mode footer behind `showHelpText`; `runWorklistTui` call site: pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` to the renderer.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new tests: chord footer hidden when `showHelpText: false`; chord footer shown when `true`/unset.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — verification only: confirm `showHelpText` default stays `true`.
- `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` — local (out-of-repo) change: set `showHelpText` to `true`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS4FJ2TX009V7V5` — "Rich settings: browseItemCount and showHelpText toggle" (completed): introduced the `showHelpText` setting for Herdr; commit `d637c9b2` gated the initial help hints but left the chord footer ungated — the root of this inconsistency.
- `WL-0MS3ANM1H007SG92` — "Rich settings for Herdr plugin: browseItemCount and showHelpText" (completed): companion/parent settings work.
- `WL-0MS31Q7FD00710B7` — "Chord shortcut system & dynamic help bar" (completed): the chord system + help bar this issue touches.
- `WL-0MQEBM6OM004Q1Q7` — "Chord dispatch and help text in browse views" (completed): chord/help-text behavior in the pi browse views (the consistency reference).
- `WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ` — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (open): separate issue on the same renderer/component (`createListRenderer`); may touch adjacent footer/list-area code.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the desired end state be? A) hint bar always shows regardless of `showHelpText` (remove/repurpose the setting); B) keep the setting and set the config to `true`; C) keep the setting and fix the inconsistency — `showHelpText` off hides *all* hints including chord-mode ones (consistent with the pi widget)."
  - Answer (operator): "C — on by default." Source: interactive reply.
  - Interpretation: keep the `showHelpText` setting; gate the chord-mode footer behind it so `false` hides all hint lines; the setting default must remain `true` (it already is in `settings.ts` `defaultSettings`, `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options — verification-only AC 3). The reporter's local config currently overrides the default to `false`, so it must be flipped to `true` (or the key removed) for the hint bar to be visible again (AC 4).
  - Note: chord key *handling* must remain functional with the footer hidden; only rendering is affected.

# Intake Brief — Insert selected work-item ID into herdr command input forms (WL-0MSGPSEFW006VINF)

## Problem statement

When typing a free-form prompt in a herdr command input form (e.g. the `P-p` chord, which opens a prompt sent to a new Pi agent pane), there is no discoverable way to reference the currently selected work item by its ID. The `<id>` magic token already works inside form field values (both chord and single-key form paths in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolve it to the selected item's ID on submit), but the behavior is undocumented, untested, and invisible in the UI — and in one edge case (no item selected, `P-p` path) a literal `<id>` leaks through to Pi.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who open the `P-p` free-form prompt (or any chord form) and want the prompt to reference the work item they currently have selected — without memorising/pasting the ID.
- **Pi agents / operators** who receive the prompt — the prompt becomes self-contained with the item ID, so no follow-up lookup is needed.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with an item selected in the worklist, I want to type `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt so the selected item's ID is inserted into the prompt sent to Pi.
- As a Herdr user filling any chord command form (e.g. `u-t` title, `u-s` stage), I want `<id>` to resolve to the currently selected item's ID the same way it does in command templates.
- As a new Herdr user, I want the form dialog to hint that `<id>` is available, so I don't need to read the README to discover it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt field inserts the currently selected work item's ID into the prompt text sent to Pi (verified by an automated regression test on the form-submit path; no new `wl` spawn needed).
2. The same `<id>`-in-field behavior works in **all** herdr command input forms, for both the chord and single-key dispatch paths.
3. The form dialog renders a discoverability hint (e.g. a footer/help line such as "type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") whenever the form is shown.
4. When no work item is selected and a form field value contains `<id>`, the behavior is graceful and consistent across all paths — no literal `<id>` is sent to Pi; the documented decision (see Risks & assumptions) is implemented and covered by a test.
5. `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `<id>`-in-form-field behavior, including the `P-p` free-prompt example.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover the free-prompt case, the generic form case, the no-item-selected edge case, and the discoverability hint.

## Constraints

- **No change to `<id>` handling in command templates** — the existing `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS` / `substituteIdentifiers` mechanism in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` stays as-is.
- **No changes to the chord definitions** in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (P-p, P-a, u-*, etc. remain bound exactly as today).
- No modal/UX overhaul of the form dialog — the hint is a minimal addition to the existing form render.
- All work tracked in wl; no changes to work-item tracking tooling.

## Existing state

- `P-p` chord → `/prompt:<prompt>` opens the command input form (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`); on submit the resulting command routes through `worklist.ts` and spawns a Pi agent pane with the bare prompt text (`stripAgentPromptPrefix` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS = {'id'}` in `form-dialog.ts` — `<id>` never triggers an unknown-identifier prompt; `substituteIdentifiers` leaves `<id>` intact in field values.
- Both form onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts` (chord-complete path ~line 2353 and single-key path ~line 2464) replace `<id>` with the selected item's ID via `flat[idx].id`.
- No regression test covers `<id>` typed inside a form field value; no UI hint; README documents `<id>` resolution for command templates only, not for field values/free prompts.
- Edge case: in the form paths, when no item is selected and the field value contains `<id>`, `finalCmd` keeps the literal `<id>` and it is sent (visible to Pi in the `P-p` case); the non-form `executeResolvedCommand` path instead returns a graceful `noop` when `<id>` is in the command and nothing is selected — inconsistent.

## Desired change

- **Verify + formalise the existing mechanism**: add regression tests asserting `<id>` in a form field value resolves to the selected item's ID, for the free prompt (P-p) and generic forms, across chord and single-key paths.
- **Discoverability**: render a hint line in the form dialog ("type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") and document the behavior in `packages/herdr/README.md` (including the `P-p` free-prompt example).
- **Graceful no-item-selected handling**: decide and implement one consistent behavior for `<id>` in field values when nothing is selected (proposed: drop the command with a toast, matching the existing `noop` convention for template `<id>`; documented in the work item).
- **No new mechanism** — the magic-token approach was chosen in intake (option a); chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts were considered and explicitly out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — render the `<id>` discoverability hint in the form dialog (footer/help line); unchanged substitution logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the two form onSubmit callbacks: consistent no-item-selected handling (drop + toast); no change to existing `<id>` resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for `<id>`-in-field resolution, the no-item-selected edge case, and the hint rendering.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `<id>` inside form field values / free prompts.

## Related work

- **Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)** — completed; introduced the `P-p` chord this feature builds on.
- **Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)** — completed; `/prompt:` routing + `send-to-pi.sh` pane spawning.
- **Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)** — completed; introduced `FormState` / form-dialog.
- **Shortcuts with multiple <id> tokens only replace the first occurrence (WL-0MRNLF5UO0088ID2)** — completed; multiple-`<id>` handling relevant to the `u-t`/`u-s` edge case.
- **Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)** — completed; text-insertion template wiring in the same code area.
- **Related work (automated report, /skill:find-related)** — additional matches retained as lower-priority context: **wl sync timeouts (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)** (completed; herdr auto-sync spawn/timeout context), **[test-failure] send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh pane-launch tests (WL-0MSGAKL8R009GB1X)** (completed; pane-launch regression relevant to the P-p spawn path), **Unify dialog widget construction and layout helpers (WL-0MNX4D4G8009XZNJ)** (completed; form-dialog rendering helpers). Automated repo-file matches (audit_runner.py, intake SKILL.md) were reviewed and dropped — generic keyword noise from the wrong repo root.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-implementation risk:** the mechanism already exists; the main risk is building a redundant insertion mechanism instead of testing + surfacing the existing magic token. Mitigation: scope is verification, discoverability, and edge-case handling only.
- **No-item-selected edge case:** proposed default = drop the command with a toast (consistent with template `<id>` noop convention). Assumption: users prefer a clear "no item selected" signal over sending a literal `<id>` to Pi.
- **Multi-`<id>` forms (`u-t` title, `u-s` stage):** typing `<id>` into such a field replaces every `<id>` in the command (target and field value) with the selected ID — existing multiple-`<id>` behavior, accepted as-is; noted in docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts (intake options b/c) are out of scope; if requested later, record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** the selected item is the one highlighted in the herdr worklist (`state.selectedIndex`), same source used by all existing `<id>` substitutions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` reference — that ID is an existing, unrelated in-progress work item (the wl read-cache epic). Which did you mean? (a) It was simply the item currently selected in your herdr pane — the feature is generic: insert *whatever* item is currently selected. (b) It should be a magic token: typing that literal string into the prompt gets replaced with the currently selected item's ID before sending. (c) Something else." — Answer (operator): "a" — generic; insert whatever item is currently selected. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Insertion mechanism — how should the ID get into the input box while typing? (a) A magic token in the prompt text (e.g. typing `<id>` — consistent with the existing placeholder convention in herdr commands). (b) A chord/keypress *inside* the input box (e.g. a key or chord that pastes the selected ID at the cursor). (c) Open the P-p prompt pre-filled with the selected ID. (d) Freeform." — Answer (operator): "a" — magic token (`<id>`). Source: interactive reply. Note: (b) and (c) explicitly out of scope.
- Q3: "Scope — which input boxes should support this? (a) Only the herdr P-p free-prompt input box. (b) All herdr command input forms. (c) Also the main pi prompt input (the `P` key in the pi TUI) — note: that lives in pi core and may not be reachable from a herdr plugin extension." — Answer (operator): "b" — all herdr command input forms. Source: interactive reply. Note: pi core input out of scope.
- Q4 (agent research note, no user answer required): does typing `<id>` in a form field already work? — Research: inspected `form-dialog.ts` (`KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS`, `substituteIdentifiers`) and both onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts`; the mechanism already resolves `<id>` to the selected item's ID on submit in both chord and single-key paths. No test covers this path; no UI hint; `P-p` with no item selected leaks literal `<id>` to Pi. Findings incorporated into Existing state / Desired change.

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Ensure Qwen is preserving thinking

**Headline:** the Qwen preserve-thinking configuration is already delivered and deployed via
`llm-manager` and `SorraAgents`; this item now holds only the outstanding live verification and
the un-configured proxy-served `qwen3` model — both owned outside ContextHub, pending a
producer decision on disposition.

> **Scope status: AWAITING PRODUCER DECISION.** Research below shows the substance of this
> item is already delivered in two sibling repositories (`llm-manager`, `SorraAgents`) and
> that ContextHub owns none of the configuration involved. Three open questions (Appendix)
> decide whether this item is closed as a duplicate, re-scoped to the outstanding live
> verification, or handed off. Nothing has been implemented from this item.

## Seed (producer's original description, preserved)

> Check to see if our Qwen config has preserve thinking enabled, see
> https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF#preserve-thinking once enabled ensure
> that our proxy modifications are not breacking it.

## Problem statement

We could not previously tell whether Qwen reasoning was being requested, preserved and
surfaced end-to-end through our local proxy. The configuration work that answers the seed
question has since landed in `llm-manager` (canonical pi overrides + proxy review + tests,
shipped in v0.1.16) and `SorraAgents` (committed pi agent config); what remains unproven is a
live, end-to-end demonstration that thinking content actually reaches a pi session
transcript for each Qwen surface — in particular the proxy-served local `qwen3` model.

## Users

- **Operator (Graham)** — wants confidence that Qwen reasoning is visible in agent
  transcripts, and to know whether the *locally served* Qwen (via our proxy) thinks at all.
  - *Story:* "As an operator, when I read an agent session transcript for a Qwen model, I can
    see its reasoning so I can audit and debug decisions."
- **Agent (Map)** — herdr-dispatched sessions run through the `Local Proxy` aliases
  (`plan`, `code`, …); reasoning must survive the proxy and the transcript round-trip.
  - *Story:* "As an agent, when my thinking is preserved I can rely on earlier reasoning
    instead of silently losing it at the proxy or on replay."
- **Maintainers of `llm-manager` / `SorraAgents`** — need a single tested source of truth for
  Qwen thinking configuration so drift is caught mechanically.
  - *Story:* "As a maintainer, a parity test fails when the live pi config diverges from the
    canonical overrides."

## Existing state (research evidence)

### pi agent model configuration (live)

`~/.pi/agent/models.json` (installed from `SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json`) contains:

| Provider | Models | Thinking configuration |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode` (anthropic-messages) | `qwen3.5-plus`, `qwen3.6-plus` | `thinkingLevelMap {off: null, high: high, max: max}` |
| `opencode-go` (openai-completions) | `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-max` | `thinkingLevelMap` + `compat.thinkingFormat: "qwen"` |
| `Local Proxy` (openai-completions, `http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1`) | `plan`, `code`, `author`, `qwen3`, `gpt120` | **none** — entries carry only `id`, so no `reasoning`, no `compat.thinkingFormat` |

- Live file is **byte-for-byte identical** (for the `modelOverrides` blocks) to the canonical
  `llm-manager/config/pi-agent/qwen-thinking-overrides.json` — verified during this intake.
- `pi-ai` semantics (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js`):
  - `thinkingFormat: "qwen"` → top-level `enable_thinking` (request-side, line ~480);
  - `thinkingFormat: "qwen-chat-template"` → `chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking, preserve_thinking: true}` (line ~483);
  - **both are gated on `model.reasoning === true`** — a model entry without it never requests thinking;
  - response-side parsing of `reasoning_content` / `reasoning` / `reasoning_text` (line ~260) is
    independent of that flag, so thinking is *displayed* if the server emits it unprompted.

### Proxy (owned by `llm-manager`)

- No code path strips `reasoning_content`: `session.py` reconstructs assistant messages with
  both `content` and `reasoning_content`; thinking-only turns emit a `"Thinking..."` content
  placeholder while the full text stays in `reasoning_content` (LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08);
  thinking-mode round-trip failures are repaired by injecting `""` (LP-0MSGU3JNU0092AFQ).
- `proxy/config.yaml` sets `summarizer_disable_thinking: true` — a **deliberate** disable of
  Qwen3 thinking for the compaction summariser to stop reasoning eating the output budget
  (LP-0MU58PBRD004OV1I), and `summarizer_reasoning_effort: minimal`.
- Proxy-level tests exist: `proxy/tests/test_qwen_thinking_preserved.py`,
  `tests/test_qwen_thinking_config.py`; contract documented in
  `llm-manager/docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md`.

### Prior delivery of this item's acceptance criteria

- `LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT` — *ensure Qwen is preserving thinking* — **completed**, closed
  "Shipped in v0.1.16"; its audit re-run recorded all four ACs met (proxy-level AC4), with a
  note that a local Qwen3 plan model once exhausted the output budget on thinking and
  truncated an audit verdict JSON.
- `SorraAgents` commit `2098144e2` — *feat: configure Qwen preserve-thinking in global model
  config (SA-0MT5RXZZ1006EW4R)*. That SA work item id is **no longer present** in the
  SorraAgents worklog store (lookup failed during this intake).

### ContextHub's own surface (this repo)

- ContextHub owns no Qwen/provider configuration. Its only proxy-adjacent client is
  `src/lib/llm.ts` (`ChatClient`, used by `wl interview` producer-review explanations) which
  posts to the same proxy with the `compact` model and consumes only the completion content —
  it ignores `reasoning_content` (the empty-content family of bugs is LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7).
- herdr dispatches pi sessions through the `Local Proxy`; this intake session itself ran as
  `Local Proxy/plan` → upstream `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, i.e. proxy routing is live here even
  though the configuration is not ours.

## Desired change (only if re-scoped — see Appendix Q1)

Close the two genuinely open gaps, in the repos that own them:

1. **Local Proxy `qwen3` thinking configuration.** Give the proxy-served Qwen an explicit
   thinking contract (`reasoning: true` + `compat.thinkingFormat: "qwen-chat-template"` for a
   llama.cpp/HF chat-template server, or a reviewed decision that the server default suffices).
2. **Live end-to-end evidence.** Demonstrate thinking content in a real pi session transcript
   for a Qwen model, cross-checked against the proxy session recording
   (`~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/`), and record the excerpts as work-item evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria (candidate — for the re-scoped variant)

- [ ] Every Qwen variant exposed by the stack (`opencode` `qwen3.5-plus`/`qwen3.6-plus`,
      `opencode-go` `qwen3.6-plus`/`qwen3.7-max`/`qwen3.7-plus`/`qwen3.8-max`, and
      `Local Proxy` `qwen3`) resolves in pi to a model that carries thinking configuration;
      the resolution is checked by a test or a documented `pi` model-listing command whose
      output is attached as comment evidence.
- [ ] The proxy-served `qwen3` model requests thinking explicitly, or a written decision
      records why the server default is sufficient; the decision names the owned file
      (`SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json` and/or
      `llm-manager/config/pi-agent/qwen-thinking-overrides.json`).
- [ ] Live verification: a pi session using a Qwen model at a non-`off` thinking level records
      thinking/reasoning content in the session transcript, and the proxy recording for the
      same turn carries `reasoning_content` on the provider→client response; redacted
      excerpts are attached to the work item.
- [ ] Automated tests cover (a) resolved thinking configuration for every exposed Qwen variant
      and (b) the absence of `reasoning_content` stripping on the proxy response path; the
      tests fail when the configuration is removed (negative control).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (`llm-manager/docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md`, `llm-manager/proxy/README.md`,
      `LOCAL_LLM.md` where proxy behaviour is described).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundaries.** pi agent configuration is owned by `SorraAgents`
  (`.pi-config/agent/models.json`, installed to `~/.pi/agent/`); the proxy is owned by
  `llm-manager`. ContextHub owns neither — no configuration edits here.
- **Preserve the deliberate thinking-off.** `summarizer_disable_thinking: true` and
  `summarizer_reasoning_effort: minimal` must stay: they are a token-budget fix, not a
  regression (LP-0MU58PBRD004OV1I).
- **`thinkingLevelMap.off` stays `null`** so an explicit "no thinking" request disables
  thinking rather than falling back to default-on.
- **No secrets in evidence**: redact API keys, tokens and host paths as needed.
- **Do not re-litigate** the `qwen` vs `qwen-chat-template` choice already settled for
  `opencode-go` (remote DashScope-style endpoint) — `qwen-chat-template` is only for local
  chat-template servers.
- **No `CHANGELOG.md` edits** — release notes are produced by the ship skill's release
  pipeline; no CI/CD pipeline tests are required by this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — context bloat / admission refusals.** `preserve_thinking: true` replays thinking in
  history, inflating prompt tokens and risking `prefill_budget_exceeded` /
  `context_too_large` refusals (`LOCAL_LLM.md`). *Mitigation:* measure before/after token use
  on a fixed prompt; keep `thinkingLevelMap.off` selectable.
- **Risk — truncated structured output.** Thinking-on by default can consume `max_tokens` and
  truncate JSON verdicts (observed during the LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT audit re-run).
  *Mitigation:* keep plan/audit aliases at explicit reasoning effort and a bounded budget.
- **Assumption.** `Local Proxy/qwen3` is served by a llama.cpp/HF chat-template Qwen3 server,
  so `qwen-chat-template` (`enable_thinking` + `preserve_thinking`) is the correct format
  rather than the remote `qwen` format — *needs producer confirmation (Q2/Q3).*
- **Assumption.** The SorraAgents work is complete under commit `2098144e2` even though work
  item `SA-0MT5RXZZ1006EW4R` is absent from that worklog store — *needs confirmation (Q1).*
- **Assumption.** The `Local Proxy` aliases used by herdr (`plan`, `code`) do not currently
  resolve to Qwen upstream: this intake session's `plan` alias served `deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
  Any live Qwen verification must therefore target `qwen3` (or an `opencode`/`opencode-go`
  Qwen model) explicitly, not an alias by assumption.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Related opportunities (e.g. making `ChatClient` tolerate
  `reasoning_content`-only responses) must be filed as separate work items, not absorbed here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `SorraAgents/.pi-config/agent/models.json` — add/adjust thinking configuration for the
  `Local Proxy` `qwen3` model entry (installed to `~/.pi/agent/models.json`).
- `llm-manager/config/pi-agent/qwen-thinking-overrides.json` — canonical overrides; extend if
  the Local Proxy variant is included.
- `llm-manager/docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md` — record the final configuration and the
  live verification procedure/evidence.
- `llm-manager/tests/test_qwen_thinking_config.py` — parity/coverage assertions for every
  exposed Qwen variant.
- `llm-manager/proxy/tests/test_qwen_thinking_preserved.py` — no-stripping and transcript
  round-trip tests.
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/session.py` — review-only unless the verification exposes a stripping gap.
- `ContextHub/src/lib/llm.ts` — read-only check that the proxy client tolerates
  `reasoning_content`-only replies (note only; likely a separate item).

## Related work

Duplicate check (performed during intake): no fully-overlapping item exists in the ContextHub
store — the only ContextHub match is this item itself. Substantive overlap lives in the sibling
stores, listed below; `LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT` carries the same four acceptance criteria and is
completed, which is why the disposition question (Q1) exists.

- `LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT` — ensure Qwen is preserving thinking (`llm-manager`, **completed**,
  shipped v0.1.16) — the same four acceptance criteria; the direct overlap for this item.
- `LP-0MU5J6J9X004UAYZ` — Docs: update thinking preservation contract.
- `LP-0MSEHOE7B005DE08` — avoid promoting thinking to content for empty responses.
- `LP-0MSGU3JNU0092AFQ` — remote 400: empty `reasoning_content` dropped on tool-call turns.
- `LP-0MU58PBRD004OV1I` — compaction summariser: minimise reasoning / disable Qwen3 thinking.
- `LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H`, `LP-0MQ6E0I06004A9G7` — `reasoning_content`-only responses and
  empty content with tool calls.
- `SorraAgents` commit `2098144e2` (work item `SA-0MT5RXZZ1006EW4R`, not found in that
  worklog store) — pi agent config for Qwen preserve-thinking.
- `WL-0MVTESPHB0021SI7`, `WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F` — ContextHub-side proxy client/classification
  work (adjacent, not overlapping).

## Potentially related docs

- `LOCAL_LLM.md` — local proxy usage, per-request priority, admission refusals.
- `llm-manager/docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md` — the current contract and verification steps.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatch routing through the proxy.

## AC coverage vs existing work

| This item's AC (from audit) | Covered elsewhere? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Qwen entries have `thinkingFormat` | Yes for `opencode`/`opencode-go`; **no** for `Local Proxy/qwen3` | live `models.json` parity with `llm-manager/config/pi-agent/qwen-thinking-overrides.json` |
| 2. Proxy does not strip thinking | Yes | `llm-manager/docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md` §2, LP-0MSGU3JNU0092AFQ; no stripping code found |
| 3. All Qwen variants reviewed | Yes for the 6 catalogued variants; `Local Proxy/qwen3` unreviewed | `qwen3.8-max` replaces the non-existent `qwen3.8-plus` |
| 4. Testing confirms thinking in transcript | **No — live evidence outstanding** | LP recorded proxy-level tests only (AC4 "Met (proxy-level)") |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Disposition of this work item (OPEN QUESTION)

The substance of this item is delivered in `llm-manager` (`LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT`, completed,
shipped v0.1.16) and `SorraAgents` (commit `2098144e2`), and ContextHub owns none of the
configuration. How should this item be disposed of?

- (a) Re-scope it to the outstanding **live end-to-end verification** (plus the `Local Proxy`
  `qwen3` gap) and run the config changes in the owning repos.
- (b) Close it as a duplicate of `LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT` and lose the residual verification.
- (c) Hand the residual work to `llm-manager` as a new `LP` item and close this one.

**Recommended:** (a) — one item keeps the residual gap and its evidence traceable here, and
the audit trail already links this item to both sibling deliveries.

Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer reply.

### Q2 — Should the proxy-served `qwen3` model request thinking explicitly? (OPEN QUESTION)

`Local Proxy/qwen3` (the local Qwen behind our proxy — the model the seed's "our proxy
modifications" most directly refers to) has no `reasoning` flag, so pi never sends
`enable_thinking`/`preserve_thinking` for it; it only surfaces `reasoning_content` if the
server emits it unprompted.

- (a) Add `reasoning: true` + `compat.thinkingFormat: "qwen-chat-template"` (owned by
  `SorraAgents`, canonical copy in `llm-manager`) and verify.
- (b) Verify only — accept the llama.cpp chat-template default and record the decision.
- (c) Out of scope: the proxy serves non-Qwen aliases in practice.

**Recommended:** (a) — it is the only path that guarantees `preserve_thinking` across turns,
and a parity test keeps it from drifting.

Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer reply.

### Q3 — How should the live verification be evidenced? (OPEN QUESTION)

- (a) Operator-run pi session with a Qwen model at thinking level `high`; redacted transcript
  excerpt plus the matching proxy recording attached as a comment.
- (b) Automated proxy-level test only (already exists) — no live session evidence.
- (c) Both: automated tests plus a one-off live transcript, recorded once and linked from the
  docs.

**Recommended:** (c) — tests prevent regression, the live transcript proves the end-to-end
path that the audit could not verify.

Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer reply.

### Research performed (agent)

- Compared the live `~/.pi/agent/models.json` overrides against
  `llm-manager/config/pi-agent/qwen-thinking-overrides.json` → identical.
- Read `pi-ai` `openai-completions` to confirm `thinkingFormat` semantics and that request-side
  thinking is gated on `model.reasoning`.
- Grepped `llm-manager/proxy` for stripping logic and summariser thinking flags; read
  `docs/qwen-thinking-preservation.md` (LP-0MT5YLL36000ZYRT contract).
- Searched ContextHub for Qwen/thinking handling: only `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`
  (pane classification) and `src/lib/llm.ts` (proxy chat client) touch the area.
- Searched the ContextHub, `llm-manager` and `SorraAgents` worklogs for duplicates and
  related items; `SA-0MT5RXZZ1006EW4R` no longer resolves in the SorraAgents store.
- Not verified (needs a live call, outside intake): whether a Qwen session currently records
  thinking parts in its transcript; whether `Local Proxy/qwen3` upstream emits
  `reasoning_content` unprompted.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66** – Feedback in interview when running LLM (completed)
- **WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY** – End-to-end verification: local-preferred deferral (busy slot → Retry-After → local completion, zero remote dispatch) (completed)
- **WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q** – Herdr isIdleStatus: prefer local_active_query over global active_query for idle detection (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absence, absent, absorbed, ac4, accept (+417 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: absent, ac4, accept, actually, add (+377 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absence, absent, accept, actually, add (+354 more)

# Leaf-aware downtime dispatch (audit tier)

## Problem statement

The downtime worker requires ALL slots free (default `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots: 0`) before any dispatch, because a parent audit's Phase 2 fan-out (1 parent + up to 2 children) needs the whole pool. But most audit candidates are **leaf items** (no children) — their audit is a single Pi session needing **1 slot**. Requiring all slots free for a leaf audit wastes partial-idle capacity (e.g. 1 or 2 of 3 slots free) that could run it locally.

This is Q5 lever 2: make the audit tier check `wl show <id> --children --json` at selection time and require fewer free slots for leaf audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Audit-tier selection (`deps.getNextAuditCandidate` or `dispatchDowntimeWork`) fetches the candidate's children (`wl show <id> --children --json`; fail-closed → treat as parent, all-slots gate).
2. **Leaf candidate** (0 children): dispatch when at least 1 slot is free (`available_slots >= 1`) for the full idle threshold.
3. **Parent candidate** (>=1 children): unchanged — all slots free (with the bounded fan-out item, effectively 2 slots needed in cheap mode, 3 in fast).
4. Same-slot stability: the "same N slots free for the full threshold" guarantee requires per-slot identity — this item is BLOCKED BY LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA (proxy exposes `slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]` in `GET /llama/local/status`). Until it lands, leaf dispatch keeps the all-slots gate (no behavior change).
5. Optional (documented, not required): the race-accepting variant — dispatch on `available_slots >= 1` without per-slot identity, accepting that an interactive request may grab the slot and the audit's first call falls back to remote. Default OFF; fail-closed philosophy preserved.
6. Tests: leaf vs parent classification, children-query failure → parent gate, per-slot idle tracking integration (reuses WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG tracker), race-accepting variant toggle.
7. README documents the leaf/parent dispatch difference and the per-slot dependency.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked-by**: LP-0MSORPUMX002LLIA (proxy per-slot details, llm worklog) — same enabler as WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG.
- **Related**: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (bounded audit fan-out — makes parent audits fit the pool, complementary); WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracker — the per-slot idle-duration machinery this item's gate consumes).
- **Related**: WL-0MSOMV6CW003OXTK (idle threshold 60s) — coordinate timing defaults.

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./downtime-worker.js` by another module remains exported from
   that exact path with identical types and values, so the 33 importing files
   compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that
   are actually used** by consumers; symbols that nothing outside the split
   modules imports are internal and need not be re-exported (producer decision
   on Q2).
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |
| 2 | Types | 617–709 | 93 |
| 3 | Idle detection | 710–862 | 153 |
| 4 | Idle-duration tracker | 863–902 | 40 |
| 5 | Per-slot idle tracker | 903–964 | 62 |
| 6 | Poller | 965–1248 | 284 |
| 7 | Dispatch (types + claim/result helpers) | 1249–2538 | 1,290 |
| 8 | Review-queue depth gate | 2539–2724 | 186 |
| 9 | Critical-only dispatch-window escape hatch | 2725–2776 | 52 |
| 10 | Herdr list-head filter dispatcher | 2777–3695 | 919 |
| 11 | Leader-election coordination dispatch | 3696–5614 | 1,919 |
| 12 | Pane-lifecycle monitor | 5615–5773 | 159 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Module-level mutable state:** `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523)

- **Pre-existing coupling:** `stalled-work.ts` imports

  imports `StalledPaneCandidate`, `StalledResumeOutcome` and `StalledScanOptions`
  types from `./stalled-work.js` — an existing type-only cycle that the split
  must not turn into a runtime cycle.
- **Precedent:** [WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO](../../../../.worklog) decomposed the
  2,584-line `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public
  API, tests passing without modification, and ≤500 lines per new module.

## Desired change

Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its contents
into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. A starting
decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision, subject to the
constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |

| `downtime-worker.constants.ts` | Tuning constants, floors/maxima, `decisionHeaderToken` | ~420 |
| `downtime-worker.types.ts` | Exported interfaces and unions (`LlamaStatus`, candidates, claim/result types, config, worker) | ~700 |
| `downtime-worker.idle.ts` | Idle detection, idle-duration tracker, per-slot tracker | ~255 |
| `downtime-worker.poller.ts` | `parseLlamaStatus`, `fetchLocalStatus`, `createDowntimePoller` | ~284 |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts` | Soft-delete/assignee holds, review-queue depth gate, audit batch status, `classifyItemForDispatch`, attempt budget, critical-only escape hatch | ~480 |
| `downtime-worker.selection.ts` | wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, rotation, critical-first, dependency frontier | ~830 |
| `downtime-worker.clamps.ts` | `clampDowntime*` settings normalisers | ~130 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.ts` | Pane args/spawn options/spawn, pane-lifecycle monitor | ~360 |
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` | Herdr list-head filter pipeline (`dispatchDowntimeWork`), prompt/comment builders | ~700–1,000 |
| `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` | `computeMostImportantItem`, `dispatchFromCoordination`, `runCoordinationCheckIn`, leader-election glue | ~1,000–1,300 (likely split into offers/leader) |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` | `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop | ~930 |
| `downtime-worker.ts` | Thin barrel re-exporting the full public surface | ~150–250 |

Where a candidate module would still exceed 1,000 lines (coordination, dispatch),
it is split further along an existing section boundary rather than left oversized.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reduce to a re-export barrel; preserve every current export.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — new; extracted constants and `decisionHeaderToken`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — new; extracted exported types/interfaces.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` — new; idle detection and trackers.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` — new; status parsing, fetch and poller.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — new; dispatchability gates and classification.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — new; wl parsers and per-tier selection.

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` — new; `createDowntimeWorker` tick loop.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts` — verify unchanged (the barrel must keep them compiling as-is).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — add a short module-layout note pointing at the new files.

## Related work

## Risks and assumptions

  AC2/AC3 make unchanged tests a hard gate.

  no cycle tooling (`madge`/`dependency-cruiser` absent; `vitest` only). Child 1
  therefore adds one **additive** test file (`downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`)
  plus a committed baseline of the 134 consumer-imported symbols, with four
  gates (public surface, single-flight, barrel/cycle, size+allowlist) and
  negative-case tests proving each gate fails when broken. This is compatible
  with AC3 ("no test file is *modified*"): nothing existing is touched.
- **D2 — the 1,000-line ceiling applies per module, not per topic.** Where a
  single concern would still exceed 1,000 lines (types, dispatch, coordination,
  orchestrator) the child splits it along an existing section boundary rather
  than compressing code. Module count is therefore not fixed; the contract is
  `wc -l ≤ 1000` for every module.
- **D3 — premise correction: the size ceiling requires `dispatchInFlightCount`
  to stay with `dispatchDowntimeWork`.** ESM imports are read-only for
  importers, so a mutated module-level `let` cannot be shared across modules
  without changing code. Child 7 keeps the declaration in
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`; the guard test enforces exactly one
  declaration.
- **D4 — the orchestrator child (9) is the only structural extraction.** The
  1,315-line `createDowntimeWorker` closes over ~30 mutable locals; getting the
  module under 1,000 lines requires lifting selected closure bodies (already
  separable: `pauseAfterPersistentErrors`, `writeCapacityStarvationSignal`,
  `recordDecision`, `batchMetadata`) and some tick phases to module scope with
  an explicit `OrchestratorContext`. Public surface and every unmodified test
  assertion are unchanged; this is recorded in the child's ACs.
  **OPEN QUESTION (producer, low urgency):** is internal context-threading
  acceptable under the "move-only" constraint for this one module, or should
  child 9 be allowed to exceed 1,000 lines with a documented exception
  (option B)? Plan-time recommendation: **A — context-threading**, because it is
  internal-only and preserves the public contract; the child proceeds on that
  basis unless the producer objects.
- **D5 — serial dependency chain.** Children are blocked in listed order rather
  than fanning out, so each landing is a single-concern diff against a known
  green tree (Q3 → A).
- **D6 — internal-only exports are permitted, barrel re-exports are not.** A
  module may export a helper so a sibling can import it; the barrel re-exports
  only the 134 consumer-used symbols (Q2 refinement). Child 10 enforces this.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-23 — Plan session (agent `herdr`): refreshed the section inventory
  (8,105 → 9,362 lines), recorded corrections to the intake brief, created 10
  child items with a serial blocking chain, recorded plan decisions D1–D6 and
  the D4 open question, and verified AC coverage across the children.
  Evidence: `wl show WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 --children --json`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session addendum)

**Q4 (verification tooling — resolved by repository inspection, no producer
answer required).** How is "no new circular imports" enforced, given there is no
`madge`/`dependency-cruiser` in the repo?

- Answer (plan agent, by inspection): no dependency-graph tool exists
  (`package.json` devDependencies: vitest, tsx, typescript, execa only). The
  guard harness (child 1) implements a static import scan instead, covering the
  barrel rule and the recorded pre-existing type-only cycle. Evidence:
  `package.json`, `scripts/` listing.
- Consequence: AC4's "dependency check" is realised as that scan.

**Q5 (test-file boundary — resolved by brief + precedent, no producer answer
required).** Parent AC3 forbids modifying test files; does adding one new guard
test file violate it?

- Answer (plan agent, by inspection of the brief): no. The brief's Risks
  section calls for "a targeted test assertion that the counter is shared", and
  AC3 forbids *modifying* existing suites (import paths, fixtures, assertions).
  The guard is additive and named separately
  (`downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`). Evidence: brief AC3 and Risks;
  precedent WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO (unchanged public API + unmodified tests).

**Q6 (current-size drift — resolved by inspection).** The brief documents 8,105
lines but the file is 9,362 lines today. Does the drift change the plan?

- Answer (plan agent, by inspection): no change of scope; the child line ranges
  and module allocations were recomputed from today's `dev`, and the extra
  `prefill-gate pacing` section plus the relocated `dispatchDowntimeWork`/pane
  sections are reflected in the child items. Evidence: `wc -l`,
  section-banner scan, declaration scan.
