# Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) measured the sync persist phase at 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline on the 123.7 MB fixture, with 78–90 % of the CPU inside `upsertFtsEntry`. `db.import()` clears every work item, re-saves every item and then re-indexes the FTS row of every item; `db.importComments()` clears every comment, re-saves every comment and re-indexes the FTS row of every item. A no-change sync therefore pays the whole cost. This item implements the fix behind parent ACs 1, 3 and 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `db.import()` writes only records whose merged value differs from the local store: unchanged work items/edges/audits are not re-saved, while `updatedAt` preservation and the later-`activityAt` merge still hold (an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted so no activity timestamp is lost).
- Records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (work items, comments, edges) and only those deleted ids have their FTS rows removed — `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` no longer force a full FTS rebuild, with existing callers (`importData()`, `doctor migrate`, `clear()`) keeping their current destructive behaviour.
- `db.importComments()` writes only changed/new comments and performs FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item ids — FTS maintenance is proportional to changed items, never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge (the delta `upsertComments()` path too: look up only the affected ids instead of scanning every item).
- Each record type is persisted inside one transaction (or batched statements): `db.importComments()` gains a transaction wrapping its clear/save/FTS work, no per-row transaction is introduced, and `db.import()`'s existing atomicity is preserved.
- Existing sync contracts still hold — delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results — and the existing sync and FTS tests plus the write-detection tests from the verification item stay green.

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertItems()`, `upsertComments()`, `hasWorkItemChanged`/`compareTrackedFields`, `mergeAuditsNewestWins`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`, `saveWorkItem`, `transaction`.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch (delta via `upsertItems`/`upsertComments`, full snapshot via `import`/`importComments`).

## Dependencies

- Verify item (persist write-detection regression tests) — test-first.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `import()`: compute the diff against the existing snapshot — unchanged records (per `hasWorkItemChanged`) are skipped entirely (no `saveWorkItem`), changed/new records are saved, ids absent from the incoming set are deleted with only their FTS rows removed; keep the transaction and `updatedAt`/`activityAt` semantics.
- In `importComments()`: diff comments by identity fields, skip unchanged saves, delete removed comments, wrap clear/save/FTS in one transaction, and re-index FTS only for the affected parent ids.
- Reduce `upsertComments()` to look up only the affected parent ids (no full table scan) and confirm no full FTS rebuild remains after a comment merge.
- Preserve `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` for their remaining callers; introduce targeted FTS-row deletion for the sync path.

## Deliverables

- Rewritten persist path: writes and FTS work proportional to actually-changed records, transactions per record type, contracts unchanged.

## Problem

The downtime dispatcher's no-dispatch decision log (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) is capped at **100 lines** (rolling). On a busy machine that is roughly **one hour** of history, because every tick that is refused for a capacity/prefill reason writes a decision entry.

During the 2026-10-22/23 overnight starvation investigation this meant the whole night could not be reconstructed: the retained window started at `2026-10-23T05:59:58Z` and the decisions for the preceding ~8 hours had already been rotated out. The pre-05:30 reasons had to be *inferred* from pi session activity instead of read from the log.

For contrast, the retained 84-minute window carried 66 no-dispatch decisions — so the cap is genuinely exhausted in about an hour of saturated polling.

## Why it matters

- Capacity-saturation starvation is silent by design (NOP), so the decision log is the **only** forensic evidence that dispatch was attempted and why it was refused.
- Post-mortem of an overnight outage ("why did almost nothing dispatch?") is currently impossible after the fact; the operator has to guess.
- The same problem affects distinguishing `capacity-saturated` / `slots-unavailable` / `prefill-cap` / `idle-age-pending` / `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` after rotation.

## Goal

As an operator, I want at least a full night (24 h) of downtime dispatch decisions to remain available on a busy machine, so that a post-mortem can report the actual terminal reasons and their counts, with bounded disk use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a machine producing decision entries at the observed rate (≥ 60/hour), at least the **last 24 hours** of `no-dispatch` decisions are readable after the fact (verified by a test that writes > 1,500 entries and asserts the oldest 24 h window is still present).
- [ ] AC2 — Disk growth is bounded: rotation happens on a documented size/time policy (e.g. daily files with a retention window, or size-based rotation with N kept), and the policy is configurable with a documented default.
- [ ] AC3 — An operator-facing, documented way exists to reconstruct a time-range summary (e.g. `wl`/herdr command, or documented `grep`/`jq` recipe over rotated files) that prints a reason tally per hour for a given night.
- [ ] AC4 — Existing readers/parsers of the single `downtime-coordination.log` path are either migrated atomically or continue to read the newest file without change; no dispatch decision is lost across a rotation boundary (test asserted).
- [ ] AC5 — Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema/observability section names the retention policy and the summary recipe.

## Evidence (2026-10-23 investigation)

- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`: 100 entries covering `2026-10-23T05:59:58.509Z` → `2026-10-23T07:13:27.061Z`.
- Reason tally in that retained window: `capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `idle-age-pending` 4, `prefill-cap` 2, `idle-age-qualified` 2 (66 no-dispatch decisions).
- Earlier overnight window (roughly `2026-10-22T21:00Z` → `2026-10-23T05:30Z`) had no retained decision records at all.

## Notes

- Related: the starvation investigation item covering long-running panes holding local-LLM capacity.
- No production behaviour change to dispatch decisions is in scope — this is observability only.

# Refactor guard: downtime-worker split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `downtime-worker.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test
file and without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: an unchanged public surface at
`./downtime-worker.js`, unmodified test files, no new circular imports, and a
single `dispatchInFlightCount` declaration. Nothing in the repo enforces these
today (there is no `madge`/`dependency-cruiser`; `vitest` is the only test
runner), so this child builds the enforcement first.

Current facts captured at plan time (2026-10-23, `dev` @ 9,362 lines):

- 36 consumer files (`src/**/*.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/*.ts`) import **134
  distinct symbols** from `./downtime-worker.js`.
- `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` is declared once (currently line 3141) and is
  mutated only inside `dispatchDowntimeWork` (lines 5772/5790/6259).
- Pre-existing cycle: `stalled-work.ts` imports values from
  `./downtime-worker.js` while `downtime-worker.ts` imports **types only** from
  `./stalled-work.js` — the one cycle the split must not widen into a runtime
  cycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree before any production code moves.
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json`
   records the 134 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation
   command, source commit, timestamp).
3. Public-surface gate: the test asserts every baseline symbol is still exported
   by `./downtime-worker.js` (value or type), so a lost re-export fails the suite.
4. Single-flight gate: exactly one production `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts`
   file (excluding `*.test.ts`/`*.fixtures.ts`) declares `dispatchInFlightCount`.
5. Barrel/cycle gate: no production `downtime-worker.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./downtime-worker.js`, and the static import graph
   of `downtime-worker*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (`stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker`, type-only).
6. Size gate: every production `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'downtime-worker.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   counter) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
8. No existing test file is modified; the change is additive only.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import ... from '.../downtime-worker.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes,
   dedupe, sort → JSON with provenance fields.
2. Write the guard test with four checks (exports, single-flight, cycle/barrel,
   size+allowlist), each as a separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
3. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   strings parsed by the same helpers) and assert each check reports a failure.
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the test file's helper section so the final
   child (barrel finalisation) can empty it in one line.
5. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Adding a test file is additive and does not violate parent AC3 ("no test file
  is modified"); the parent brief's Risks section explicitly calls for "a
  targeted test assertion" to enforce AC5.
- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

   mutated in that module only (current lines 5772/5790/6259), so no

   passes. `dispatchInFlightCount` is NOT re-exported.

   dispatched marker → free-slot minimums → active-audit single-flight →

  `readOwnHeadWindow`, `dispatchFromOwnHead`,
  `dispatchFromCoordinationGated`, `runCoordinationCheckIn`,
  `logHostAuditSaturation`.

Do not change offer file semantics (one offer per instance, file-order
dispatch, re-validation at dispatch time via `fetchItem` →
`classifyItemForDispatch`), the retired-tier note, cross-root ordering
removal, or check-in cadence logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both new modules exist and are ≤1,000 lines; if
   `coordination-leader.ts` would still exceed 1,000 lines it is split further
   along an existing section boundary (e.g. gated dispatch vs. check-in) rather
   than left oversized; the guard size gate passes with the allowlist unchanged.
2. Every consumer-imported symbol keeps its name, signature and behaviour and is
   re-exported by the barrel (`computeMostImportantItem`,

3. Coordination applies the same neutral non-terminal cooldown and

# Extract downtime-worker orchestrator modules

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Source range (current `dev`, 9,362 lines):** worker orchestrator 6637–8189 (`DowntimeWorkerConfig`/`DowntimeWorkerTickResult`/`DowntimeWorker` types move to the types module; `createDowntimeWorker` ~1,315 lines stays the extraction target)
**New modules:** `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` (factory + returned object), `downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` (tick phases, cooldown/three-strike state machine, decision logging, starvation signal)

## Goal

As a downtime-dispatch maintainer, I want the per-tick orchestrator split into a
factory module and named tick-phase helpers, so that the tick loop is readable in
one pass and a tick-phase change does not require holding the 1,300-line
closure in view.

## Scope

This is the one child where pure relocation is not sufficient: the 1,315-line
`createDowntimeWorker` closes over ~30 mutable locals (`dispatching`,
`lastDispatchAt`, `activeAuditBatch`, `cooldownUntil`, `errorStrikes`,
`lastDecisionReason`, `starvationTracker`, `leaderManager`, …), so reducing the
module below 1,000 lines requires lifting selected closure bodies to module
scope with an explicit shared-state/context parameter. **Public surface must not
change:** `createDowntimeWorker` keeps its exact signature, the returned
`DowntimeWorker` object keeps every property, getter and method (`idleSince`,
`dispatching`, `lastDispatchAt`, `isLeader`, `instanceId`, `enabled`,
`override`, `restoredFromMarker`, `toggle`, `tick`, …) with identical
observable behaviour.

Allowed in this child only:

- Moving the already-separable inner helpers to module scope with an explicit
  parameter: `pauseAfterPersistentErrors` (~7007), `writeCapacityStarvationSignal`
  (~7065), `recordDecision` (~7127), `batchMetadata` (~7203).
- Extracting tick phases that take the context object as their first argument
  (poll/evaluate, pane monitor + close reaper, cooldown evaluation, dispatch
  attempt, decision logging).
- A `type OrchestratorContext` (internal, not re-exported) describing the shared
  state.

Not allowed: changing tick order, cadence, cooldown/three-strike thresholds,
leader/check-in sequencing, log lines, or any exported type.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` and `-orchestrator-tick.ts` exist and each
   is ≤1,000 lines; the guard size gate passes with the allowlist unchanged
   (still only `downtime-worker.ts`).
2. `createDowntimeWorker` keeps its exact exported signature and returns an
   object with the identical public members; the split-guard public-surface gate
   passes and `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` (2,230 lines) passes
   **unmodified**.
3. No new public symbol is added to the barrel: `OrchestratorContext` and the
   extracted phase helpers are internal module exports at most, never
   re-exported (Q2 refinement).
4. The extracted helpers perform no logic change: the no-candidate cooldown
   (default 60 min), the three-strike CLI-error rule
   (`DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT`), in-flight guarding, leader/check-in ordering
   before the cooldown gate, and the immediate pause cancellation on a
   successful re-offer all behave identically.
5. `dispatchInFlightCount` is **not** consulted or re-declared here; the
   single-flight gate still passes (the counter stays in
   `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts`).
6. The unmodified suites `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`,
   `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `slot-budget-machine.test.ts`,
   `migration-machine.test.ts`, `long-running-panes.test.ts` pass, plus the full
   `packages/herdr` suite (`/skill:test`).
7. Module doc comments name each single responsibility; moved banners and
   work-item provenance comments travel with the code.
8. `git diff` shows relocation, import rewiring and the documented context
   threading only — no change to a decision, threshold or log message.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a characterisation test **first** for any tick branch that the existing
   orchestrator suite does not pin (cooldown cancellation, strike reset,
   starvation signal emission).
2. Move the four already-separable inner helpers to `orchestrator-tick.ts` with
   an explicit `ctx` parameter; keep behaviour identical.
3. Extract tick phases one at a time, running the orchestrator suite after each
   move (move → test → next move), so a regression is attributable.
4. Leave `createDowntimeWorker` in `orchestrator.ts` as the composition point;
   rewire monolith/barrel imports.
5. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope) + guard suite.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — remove moved blocks, add re-exports
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — read-only gate (must stay unmodified)

## Dependencies

Blocked by: coordination child. Blocks: barrel-finalisation child.

## Notes

Parent AC3 is "behaviour-preserving, move-only". Extracting closure bodies into
context-taking module functions is a **structural** change to non-exported
internals — the minimum needed to satisfy AC1 (≤1,000 lines/module) for this
module. The public `DowntimeWorker` contract and all unmodified test assertions
are the behavioural gate; the approach was reviewed at plan time and recorded in
the parent's plan notes (recommended option A).

# Finalise downtime-worker barrel and docs

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Scope:** the residual `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` content (module doc comment + import/export wiring) plus the documentation updates and the final verification pass for the epic.

## Goal

As a consumer of the downtime worker, I want `downtime-worker.ts` to be a thin,
honest barrel that re-exports exactly the symbols other modules actually use, and
I want the dispatcher docs to show the module layout, so that the public surface
is discoverable and the epic's acceptance criteria are verifiable in one pass.

## Scope

- Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to: module-level doc comment (kept provenance,
  trimmed to a short overview + pointer to the module layout), and
  `export … from './downtime-worker.*.js'` statements only.
- Re-export **only symbols actually imported by consumers** (134 baseline symbols
  captured by the split-guard child); stop re-exporting symbols no consumer and
  no sibling module uses.

  exports), update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it names internals, and fix any

- Record the final verification evidence on the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wc -l packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ≤ 250, and the file contains no
   function/type/const declarations — only the doc comment and re-exports.
2. The barrel re-exports exactly the 134 consumer-imported symbols from the
   baseline, and no symbol that neither a consumer nor a sibling module imports;

   imports) is recorded as evidence.
3. `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is empty and the split-guard test proves every
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts` production module (including the
   barrel) is ≤1,000 lines; the allowlist-shrink assertion is satisfied.

# Reservation handshake fixtures and contract tests (test-first slice)

## Summary

Pin the local-proxy reservation handshake as exported TypeScript types,
fixtures and contract tests **before** any client code exists, so the reserve
client (C2) and the one-per-idle-window guard (C3) are built against pinned,
tolerant-parsing behaviour and a red-then-green test contract.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC1** (reserve client) — the granted/refused shapes and their
  parsing are pinned here; the client itself lands in C2.
- Parent **AC2** (failure-mode backcompat) — the absent/500/timeout fixtures
  that C2's fail-open path is tested against are defined here.

## Target outcome

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` and a new
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` describe the reservation
contract from the parent description:

- `POST {proxyUrl}/llama/local/reserve` request: the pane's expected token
  size, priority and cache state.
- Granted response: gate ticket id + TTL, surfaced as
  `X-Local-Reservation` on the pane's first request.
- Refused response: HTTP 429 with `{ reason, retry_after_s }`
  (reasons such as `reserved-fallback`, `prefill-gate`, `queue-full`).
- Endpoint absent (404) / server error (500) / hang → fail-open `null`
  (today's polling behaviour), never a throw.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C1-AC1 — types and constants.** Exported reservation types
   (`LocalReservationRequest`, granted/refused result shapes) and header-name
   constants (`X-Local-Reservation`, plus the `X-Local-Preference` /
   `X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` names used by C4) live in
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (or a small dedicated module
   re-exported from it) and are importable by tests.
- **C1-AC2 — fixtures.** `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` gains
   `reserveGranted`, `reserveRefused429`, `reserveEndpointAbsent`,
   `reserveServerError` and `reserveTimeout` built in the established
   `prefillPacingStatus()` style (typed, commented, no ad-hoc inline objects
   in tests).
- **C1-AC3 — contract tests (red first).** `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`
   asserts: granted body → typed ticket with a finite TTL; 429 body → typed
   refusal with `reason` and `retry_after_s`; non-JSON/garbage body,
   missing ticket, negative/non-finite `retry_after_s` → fail-open `null`;
   404/500/timeout → fail-open `null` with no throw. Tests are written before
   the parser and fail against the current tree.
- **C1-AC4 — traceability.** Each test name cites the parent AC it serves
   (`AC1` / `AC2`) so the C3 and C5 reviews can trace coverage.
- **C1-AC5 — no behaviour change.** No production dispatch behaviour changes
   in this slice (`downtime-worker.*` tests other than the new file stay
   green); the parser is exported but not yet called on the dispatch path.

## Dependencies

- **None** (blocking parent only). This is the test-first slice that C2/C3 build on.

## Constraints

- The proxy item (llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`) is **not yet implemented
  or present in the llm-manager worklog** (verified 2026-10-23: no
  `llama/local/reserve` handler in `proxy/`). Pin the contract exactly as
  documented in the parent description; keep parsing strict-but-tolerant so
  additive proxy fields cannot break us.
- Reuse the existing fixture/parse patterns (schema-v2 `LlamaStatus`,
  `parseOptionalCount`, fail-closed `null` semantics).
- No new polling loop; the reserve client introduced in C2 piggybacks the
  single-flight status poll.

## Risky assumptions

- Ticket TTL and the exact granted-body field names are unknown until the
  proxy lands — mitigation: tolerant parsing + a single typed accessor, so a
  rename is a one-line change.
- The refusal reasons enumerated in the parent (`reserved-fallback`,
  `prefill-gate`, `queue-full`) may not be exhaustive — mitigation: accept
  any non-empty string reason, never branch on an unknown one.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reservation types, header
  constants, tolerant parser.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — reservation fixtures.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts` — new contract tests.

## Deliverables

- Reservation types, header constants and parser (exported, unused on the
  dispatch path).
- Fixtures for granted / refused / absent / 500 / timeout.
- Contract tests, red before the parser and green after it.

# Reserve client with fail-open dispatch gate

## Summary

At each dispatch decision the worker calls `POST {proxyUrl}/llama/local/reserve`
on the existing single-flight poll cadence: a granted ticket releases the
pane spawn (ticket forwarded to the pane so its first request carries
`X-Local-Reservation`); a 429 refusal defers with `retry_after_s` and records
the refusal; an absent/500/timeout endpoint degrades to exactly today's
polling behaviour. The decision log gains the reservation evidence.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC1** (reserve client) — implementation of the reserve call, the
  granted→launch / refused→defer paths.
- Parent **AC2** (failure-mode backcompat) — absent/500/timeout → today's
  polling behaviour, covered by tests.
- Parent **AC4** (decision-log evidence, dispatch half) — ticket state,
  `admit`, `projected_wait_s`, `retry_after_s` recorded per decision.

## Target outcome

The dispatcher never launches without a ticket: it asks, gets a ticket, then
launches — never poll-then-hope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C2-AC1 — reserve client (parent AC1).** when the proxy serves the reserve endpoint (fixture), a dispatch first receives a ticket and only then launches with the reservation header; a refused ticket defers with `retry_after` and is recorded (`downtime-worker.mock.test.ts`-style mocked fetch, following the existing fixture pattern).
   Concretely: the spawned pane receives the granted ticket (env
   `PI_LOCAL_RESERVATION_TICKET`, forwarded by `send-to-pi.sh` /
   `run-pi-agent.sh`) so its first request carries `X-Local-Reservation`.
- **C2-AC2 — refusal recorded.** The proxy's refusal reason
   (`reserved-fallback` / `prefill-gate` / `queue-full`) is carried into the
   decision entry with `retry_after_s` and a distinct header token via
   `decisionHeaderToken`, and the spawn path never runs.
- **C2-AC3 — failure mode backcompat (parent AC2).** endpoint absent/500/timeout → exactly today's polling behaviour, no crash, no stuck pane (tests for each): one test per failure mode (404 / 500 / timeout), each asserting dispatch proceeds as if the reserve endpoint did not exist, with no retry storm.
- **C2-AC4 — decision-log evidence (parent AC4, dispatch half).** Every
   polled decision entry records `reservationTicket` (id, granted at),
   `admit` (true/false), `projectedWaitS` and `retryAfterS` via the extended
   `DecisionEntryFields`.
- **C2-AC5 — no new polling (parent constraint).** The reserve call rides the
   existing single-flight poll cadence — a test asserts at most one reserve
   request per poll and no standalone timer/poll loop.
- **C2-AC6 — pacing preserved (parent constraint).** Pacing only reduces
   concurrency: the reserve call never raises the free-slot budget and never
   bypasses the fail-closed `slots-unavailable` / `capacity-saturated` /
   prefill gates (regression tests stay green).

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** C1 (reservation fixtures + contract tests).
- **Blocks:** C3 (race guard) and C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- Reservation piggybacks the status-poll cadence (no new polling loop).
- Fail-open: an older proxy (no reserve endpoint) is fully supported.
- Surgical: extends `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`'s pacing with the atomic claim;
  does not rewrite the dispatcher.
- Ticket TTL bound: a granted ticket that cannot be forwarded to the pane
  (spawn failure) must be treated as released/expired, never leaked.

## Risky assumptions

- The exact ticket field names/TTL come from the C1 pinned contract; a rename
  in the proxy lands as a one-line accessor change.
- Reservation latency per dispatch is acceptable (parent calls it out) — the
  C2-AC5 test asserts call-count bounds so latency cannot silently grow.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `fetchLocalReservation`,
  dispatch-gate wiring, decision-log fields.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` / `.reserve.test.ts` /
  `.test.ts` — reserve + backcompat + call-count tests.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — ticket
  env passthrough to the pane.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — reservation
  handshake + ticket forwarding documented (parent AC5 partial).

## Deliverables

- `fetchLocalReservation` client + dispatch-gate integration (granted/refused/
  fail-open), runner ticket passthrough, decision-log evidence fields,
  tests, doc sections.

# One-per-idle-window reservation race guard

## Summary

Assert and enforce the operator requirement that an idle window produces
**at most one** launch: after a ticket-backed launch no further pane starts
until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight <
local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** a new reservation is granted for that
specific launch. Pin the same-tick two-instance race with a test.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC3** (one-per-idle-window) — the whole slice.

## Target outcome

Two herdr instances observing the same idle window cannot both launch; the
loser defers with the proxy's own refusal evidence instead of queueing a
doomed pane that later falls back to remote.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C3-AC1 — one-per-idle-window (parent AC3).** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
   The test runs two `createDowntimeWorker` instances against one mock proxy in
   the same tick and asserts exactly one pane is spawned, the second dispatch
   refused by the reservation call.
- **C3-AC2 — post-launch suppression (parent AC3).** After a successful
   launch, no second pane launches on later ticks while
   `local_prefills_in_flight >= local_max_concurrent_prefills`; only a fresh
   status tick with headroom **and** a ticket granted for that specific launch
   permits another spawn.
- **C3-AC3 — losing-instance evidence (parent AC4, dispatch evidence).** The
   losing instance's decision entry records the refusal reason,
   `retry_after_s` and `admit: false`, with a header token distinguishable
   from `prefill-cap`/`prefill-gate` so an operator can tell a lost race from
   a paced stop.
- **C3-AC4 — coordination-path parity.** The same one-per-idle-window rule
   holds on the coordination-leader dispatch path
   (`dispatchFromCoordination`) — no second launch in the same idle window
   there either (test).
- **C3-AC5 — no regression.** The guard never admits a dispatch the per-slot /
   saturated / prefill gates would refuse and never changes single-instance
   behaviour when the proxy grants normally (existing `downtime-worker.*`
   suites stay green).
- **C3-AC6 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the one-per-idle-window rule
   and how it composes with the existing coordination leader.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** C2 (reserve client + dispatch gate).
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The proxy is the arbiter (atomic reservation grant); herdr does **not** add
  a second distributed lock — it only refuses to launch without its own
  granted ticket.
- Never raise the concurrency budget; never bypass the fail-closed per-slot
  handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Reuse the C2 reserve client; no duplicate reservation code path.

## Risky assumptions

- The proxy grants at most one ticket per idle window across instances
  (stated contract). If it instead grants N tickets for N slots, the guard
  still holds for the serialised default (`cap = 1`); the `cap > 1` case
  intentionally permits `cap` concurrent launches, matching prefill headroom.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — launch/refusal guard state on the
  tick and on `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` /
  `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` / new race test file — race and
  suppression tests (file chosen at implementation time).
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Deliverables

- In-flight launch guard, same-tick race test, coordination-path parity test,
  refusal-evidence decision entries, doc sections.

# Per-turn local preference and route logging

## Summary

Give agent panes a per-turn capacity claim: a pi extension injects
`X-Local-Preference` (`local-only` for work the operator marks local-first,
`remote-ok` for background work) on the Local Proxy provider path and records
`X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers into a route log,
so a refusal is immediate and honest instead of a silent 120 s proxy-side
wait. The herdr runner sets the preference per spawn from a policy knob.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC4** (per-turn preference) — the whole slice (the dispatch-side
  decision evidence is delivered by C2-AC4).

## Target outcome

An agent turn either gets a local route or receives an immediate, recorded
fallback decision; the operator can read per-session route evidence next to
the dispatch decision log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C4-AC1 — per-turn preference (parent AC4).** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
   Concretely: the herdr agent runner (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` /
   `run-pi-agent.sh`) sets the preference for each spawn from a policy knob
   (proposed `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` env / herdr setting
   `downtimeLocalPreference`, default `local-only` for downtime panes and
   `remote-ok` for background/scheduled work); the extension sends that value
   on every proxied request and writes one JSONL route line per turn to the
   bounded route log; pure-module and runner-script tests assert both values
   and the unset (no header) case.
- **C4-AC2 — route log detail.** Each route line carries session id,
   timestamp, route, fallback reason and model, appended to a bounded log
   (proposed `.worklog/local-route.log`, rolling convention like
   `downtime-dispatches.log`, capped at 2000 entries). Absent or malformed
   headers write no entry and never throw.
- **C4-AC3 — fail-open backcompat.** With no knob set, no headers from an
   older proxy, or the extension absent, requests are byte-identical to
   today's (no header, no log, no behaviour change); a capture failure never
   breaks a turn (tests).
- **C4-AC4 — dispatch correlation.** Route-log entries carry the pi session
   id and the reservation ticket (when one was forwarded), so a dispatcher
   decision can be correlated with the turns it produced (test + doc).
- **C4-AC5 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the preference policy knob and
   the route log, with matching code comments.

## Dependencies

- **None** inside this item — independent of C1–C3 (separate pi extension +
  runner path) and can run in parallel; it only shares the contract header
  names pinned in C1.
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The pi extension is the only place that can see the response headers (pi
  owns the request path); reuse the established extension pattern
  (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-sse-signals` wraps the Local Proxy provider's
  `streamSimple` with a capturing fetch) and the repo installer
  (`scripts/install-pi-extension.sh`).
- Fail-open only: a missing preference knob or a broken extension must never
  block or alter a turn.
- No new polling loop; route logging is per response.
- No secrets/PII in the route log.

## Risky assumptions

- Pi's provider override can inject a request header and read response
  headers (precedent: `proxy-sse-signals` reads the body stream via a
  capturing fetch; the same wrapper exposes `Response.headers`).
- The route log location is acceptable as a per-root `.worklog/` artifact
  (same convention as the existing downtime logs); confirm at implementation
  if the producer prefers `~/.pi/agent/logs/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (producer):** is `local-only` the right default for downtime
panes (fail fast to remote) vs a wait-for-local default? Default proposed from
the parent's "work the operator marks local-first" wording; the knob makes it
configurable either way.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` (new provider wrapper)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` (new pure
  module, unit-testable without pi) — precedent
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `shared/run-pi-agent.sh`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (env/knob plumbing),
  `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (knob default + clamp).
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Deliverables

- Local-preference pi extension + tests, runner/knob plumbing, bounded route
  log writer, doc sections.

# Worktree `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist`

## Problem statement

In an `implement.py` worktree, every `@worklog/shared` import (tests, `src/**`,
spawned CLI subprocesses) resolves through the worktree's `node_modules`
symlink to the **main checkout's** `packages/shared/dist`, so a branch that
changes `packages/shared/src/**` is invisible to the build/test gate: correct
new code fails (false red) and a genuinely broken shared change can pass
(false green).

## Users

**Primary:** agents (and the humans reviewing their work) running the implement
workflow in a worktree on this repo.

- As an agent implementing a work item that touches `packages/shared/src/**`,
  I want the sanctioned gate to exercise the code in my worktree, so that a
  green result means my change is correct and a red result names my change.
- As a producer reviewing an `in_review` item, I want the gate result in the
  work-item record to be trustworthy, so that I am not approving a false green
  or debugging a false red.
- As an agent starting a fresh worktree, I want the supported setup to be one
  documented command (or automatic), so that I do not rediscover the
  `rsync` workaround — or "fix" the symptom by weakening tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gate observes worktree code.** From a fresh worktree whose branch changes
   `packages/shared/src/**`, the sanctioned gate
   (`python3 $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --scope full`,
   and the same command as invoked by `implement.py finish`) exercises the
   worktree's shared code — proven by a probe change in the worktree that the
   gate observes (and that an unmodified main checkout would not satisfy).
2. **Resolution is inspectable.** A repo-local check reports the resolved
   `@worklog/shared` package root for the current checkout and asserts it is
   the current worktree's `packages/shared`; covered by an automated test.
3. **No cross-checkout contamination.** No writes pass through the
   `node_modules` symlink into the main checkout's `node_modules`; after
   start → build → gate → finish from a worktree, the main checkout remains
   git-clean apart from gitignored build artefacts.
4. **Stale resolution cannot fail silently.** Either the refresh happens
   automatically or start/finish surfaces an actionable warning (or failure)
   naming the stale `packages/shared/dist` path — behaviour covered by a test
   for the detection helper.
5. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (also resolving the
   dangling reference in `AGENTS.md`) documents the module-resolution order,
   the supported way to make `packages/shared` changes visible in a worktree,
   and the stale-dist failure signature (e.g. the WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO
   "spy never called" symptom).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **`implement.py` is not in this repository.** The implement skill scripts
  live in SorraAgents (`~/.pi/agent/skills -> /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`).
  A change to `implement.py start`/`finish` needs a SorraAgents (`SA-`) work
  item; this `WL-` item can only commit ContextHub-side artefacts (scripts,
  docs, `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/`). **Q1 below decides the split.**
- **`npm install` inside a worktree is forbidden** by the implement skill:
  writes would pass through the `node_modules` symlink and corrupt the shared
  tree. Any option that installs into the worktree is out of bounds.
- **No writes through the `node_modules` symlink** into the main checkout's
  `node_modules` (AC3).
- **The live `wl` CLI executes the main checkout's `dist`**: `wl` →
  `<project>/dist/cli.js` → `@worklog/shared` → main `packages/shared/dist`.
  Refreshing that `dist` from a worktree changes what every concurrent agent
  and producer runs mid-flight (and a half-built worktree would ship into live
  tooling), so the `rsync`-into-main workaround is a fallback, never the
  default fix.
- **Concurrency:** several worktrees may build at once; any solution that
  mutates shared state (`dist`, `node_modules`) must serialise or be avoided.
- **Do not weaken tests** to make the gate pass; a shared-change item that
  fails the gate must fail loudly (this is the exact failure mode observed in
  WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO).
- Behaviour change must stay confined to worktree setups: the main checkout's
  build/test/gate behaviour must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Existing state

- `implement.py start` symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules ->
  <main-checkout>/node_modules` (`_ensure_node_modules_symlink`, SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B)
  and mirrors nested/workspace `node_modules` directories
  (`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`, OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT).
- Verified this session: the main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` is
  a relative symlink `../../packages/shared`, i.e. the main checkout's package;
  `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` point at `./dist/*.js`
  (gitignored build output); `npm run build:shared` builds the **worktree's**
  `packages/shared/dist`, which no worktree import resolves to.
- `vitest.config.ts` excludes `**/.worklog/worktrees/**` from discovery (so
  worktree test files are not double-collected), but that does not affect
  module resolution of the shared package.
- Project-local implement extension hooks exist: `implement.py start` surfaces
  `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/SKILL_PREFIX.md`; `SKILL_POSTFIX.md` is
  surfaced by `finish`. Today only `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`
  exists in this repo.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` does **not** exist although `AGENTS.md`
  links to it (dangling reference); the closest document is
  `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`, which covers the
  missing-`node_modules` failure (not this one).
- Prior manual workaround (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO): build `packages/shared` in the
  worktree, then `rsync -a --delete packages/shared/dist/
  <main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist/` before running the gate.

## Desired change

Make `@worklog/shared` resolve to the **worktree's own** `packages/shared`
(whose `dist` the worktree build produces), or — as the minimum acceptable
outcome per the original ACs — make the stale resolution loud and documented.
Candidate mechanisms:

| Option | Mechanism | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Worktree-local link farm** (recommended) | `start` builds `<worktree>/node_modules` as a real directory of symlinks to each main-checkout entry (nested scope dirs like `@worklog` materialised with per-package symlinks; `.bin` linked as a whole), overriding `@worklog/shared -> <worktree>/packages/shared` | Per-worktree isolation; no shared-state mutation; keeps `npm install` prohibition intact; fixes tests, `src/**` and spawned subprocesses alike | Touches the sanctioned symlink model (docs/implement skill must change); needs refresh when the main checkout's dependency set changes; extra moving parts in `implement.py` |
| **B. Automated dist refresh** | After `build:shared` in the worktree, `rsync` the worktree `packages/shared/dist` into the main checkout's `dist` under a lock | Small, matches the proven manual workaround | Mutates the checkout that the live `wl` CLI and every other worktree execute; concurrent worktrees clobber each other; a half-built branch reaches live tooling |
| **C. Detection + actionable warning only** | Detect that the worktree changed `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` resolves outside the worktree; warn (or fail) naming the stale dist path; document the workaround | Lowest risk; satisfies the original "either automatic or actionable warning" clause; no resolution change | Does not satisfy AC1 (gate still not exercising worktree code) |
| **D. Node resolution hook** (`NODE_OPTIONS`/loader, tsconfig `paths`) | Map `@worklog/shared` to the worktree package at runtime/typecheck | No filesystem changes | Invasive and platform/loader fragile; tsx/vitest/spawned subprocess coverage unequal; `rootDir` conflicts |

Recommended shape: **A for resolution** (delivered as a SorraAgents change to
`implement.py start`, plus a ContextHub-side equivalent script so the fix is
usable immediately and testable here), with **C as the safety net** so a
missed refresh is loud rather than silent. The ContextHub side also delivers
the docs (AC5) and the resolution check (AC2).

> **Assumption (pending Q1/Q2):** the executable fix is split — SorraAgents
> owns the automatic `implement.py` behaviour; ContextHub owns the reusable
> script, the extension hook, the docs and the tests that verify the behaviour
> end-to-end from this repo.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/package.json` — `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js`; the reason a build output (not `src`) is what resolves.
- `node_modules/@worklog/shared` — main checkout's relative symlink `../../packages/shared` (the stale hop).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1638), `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` (~L1735), `run_build` (+`finish` build step ~L4432); the natural place for an automatic refresh/detection (SorraAgents repo).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md` — worktree `node_modules` contract and the "do NOT run `npm install` in a worktree" constraint (~L547–558).
- `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/SKILL_PREFIX.md` — new, project-local instruction surfaced by `implement.py start` (immediate mitigation hook).
- `scripts/` — new worktree shared-link/check script (name TBD, e.g. `scripts/worktree-shared-link.mjs`), plus a test under `tests/unit/`.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — new doc (also referenced by `AGENTS.md`); update `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` to cross-reference it.
- `vitest.config.ts` — worktree exclusion (context only; unchanged unless a resolution check needs it).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` — existing precedent for replacing a stale `@worklog/shared` copy with a live symlink (pattern to follow).

## Provenance

- discovered-from: WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO

## Related work

- **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** (Verify: persist write-detection regression tests) — discovered-from; hit the false-red symptom and used the manual `rsync` workaround.
- **WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q** (Herdr selection-list pane crashes on startup when vendored `@worklog/shared` artifacts are stale) — same class of defect (stale build artefact behind a package resolution), different path (`packages/herdr/node_modules` packaged copy); its notes explicitly flag *this* worktree-isolation gap as tracked separately.
- **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** (implement.py worktrees lack node_modules) — established the current `node_modules` symlink behaviour and its verification doc; this item is the direct successor risk of that design.
- **WL-0MSRG481O007QVEA** (install-herdr.sh links plugin to worktree path) — precedent for worktree-path linkage bugs.
- **WL-0ML0IFVW00OCWY6F** (Fix `wl init` to support git worktrees) — worktree support context.
- SorraAgents **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** (auto-symlink `node_modules` into implement worktrees) and **OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT** (nested `node_modules` symlinks) — the behaviours that create the stale-resolution hop.
- Prior art: `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` (`linkSharedPackage()`), which replaced a packaged copy with a relative symlink to the live workspace package.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — false green is worse than false red.** Weakening tests would "fix"
  the false red and leave the false green; the item must guard against that
  (review check: no test changes that reduce assertions in shared-dependent
  tests).
- **Risk — link farm drift.** Materialising `node_modules` entries at `start`
  time means dependencies added to the main checkout later are missing from
  long-lived worktrees; mitigation: idempotent re-run of the link step plus a
  detection warning.
- **Risk — live `wl` contamination** if option B is chosen; it changes the
  shared `dist` that every agent's `wl` executes. Must not be the default.
- **Risk — concurrent worktrees.** Any shared-state mutation needs a lock;
  option A avoids the issue entirely.
- **Risk — cross-repo coordination.** If the fix needs `implement.py` changes,
  the SorraAgents item must land (and be released) before this item can verify
  end-to-end; the ContextHub script keeps the fix usable in the interim.
- **Assumption —** `dist/` remains gitignored in the main checkout, so build
  artefacts never make it dirty (verified in the source description).
- **Assumption —** agents run the sanctioned gate via the test skill from the
  worktree root, so `run_tests.py`'s project-root detection targets the
  worktree.
- **Scope-creep watch:** the same resolution hop affects `packages/herdr`
  (already handled by `link-shared.mjs`) and any future workspace package;
  record follow-ups as linked work items rather than widening this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (OPEN QUESTION): Where should the executable fix live — SorraAgents
  `implement.py`, a ContextHub-local script + implement extension, both, or
  warning-only? — Answer: *pending producer*. Options and recommendation in
  the interview round below; affects AC1/AC4 wording and the blocking
  relationship with a new `SA-` item.
- Q2 (OPEN QUESTION): Which resolution mechanism — worktree-local link farm (A),
  automated `rsync` of shared `dist` into the main checkout (B), or detection
  + actionable warning only (C)? — Answer: *pending producer*.
- Q3 (OPEN QUESTION): Should `implement.py finish` hard-fail (not merely warn)
  when the worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared`
  still resolves outside the worktree? — Answer: *pending producer*.
- Duplicate-work check performed (`wl search "worktree shared dist node_modules
  symlink"`, 15 hits reviewed): no duplicate — WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q is the
  `packages/herdr` packaged-copy variant (completed), WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2 is
  the missing-`node_modules` failure (completed), and this item's acceptance
  criteria (gate exercises worktree shared code + isolation + docs) are not
  satisfied by either. Source: `wl show` on both, plus
  `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ.md`.
- Research (verified in this session): the resolution chain
  `worktree/node_modules -> main/node_modules/@worklog/shared ->
  main/packages/shared` and `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` →
  `./dist/database.js`; `implement.py` `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` /
  `run_build`; the implement skill's "do NOT `npm install` in a worktree"
  contract; the project-local `SKILL_PREFIX.md` surfacing hook; the missing
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (dangling `AGENTS.md` link). Sources:
  file reads above, `implement.py` lines ~1638/~1735/~4432, `SKILL.md`
  ~L547–558.

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

## Summary

`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` in this repo has no `syncAllowedAuthors` list, so `wl sync` runs the author-identity gate in strict mode: it refuses to merge any incoming commit on `refs/worklog/data` whose author email differs from the store's `git config user.email`. The shared ref carries 3,687 commits authored by `pi@local` while this checkout's `user.email` is `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, so agent-initiated `wl sync` runs here were refused and needed `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Fix (as shipped)

Declare a narrow allow-list in `.worklog/config.yaml` — **not** in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`: that file is this repository's project *template* (`projectName: TestProject`, `prefix: TEST`), so identities listed there would leak into every project created from it.

```yaml
syncAllowedAuthors:
  - 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
  - pi@local
```

Never use `null`/`true` (allow-all); empty-author commits must stay refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The effective `syncAllowedAuthors` (defaults merged with `.worklog/config.yaml`) lists both identities, and `config.yaml` never shadows a defaults entry with a narrower list.
- [x] `wl sync` and `wl sync --dry-run` succeed in this checkout without `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [x] A guard test drives the real config merge and the real gate: listed authors accepted, unknown author refused, empty author refused even with the allow-all override (`tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes — blocked by `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts`, already red on `dev` before this change (9 failures, introduced by commit `0d8324df`); triaged as `WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0`.

## Observed

Found while filing WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J (prefix rename request) on 2026-10-24; the first sync was completed with `--allow-foreign-author` as a one-off, then `git pull` was run and `wl sync` re-tested.

# If Critical item is a child it should not show in top level herdr selection list (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist renders critical-priority work items that have a `parentId` at the **top level** of the selection list, even when their parent is also listed — so a critical child appears twice: once as a standalone top-level row and once under its parent when expanded. The top level should contain only root items; a critical child must appear only as a child.

Confirmed live reproduction: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`, parent `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`) is a child of `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (critical, in-progress). Both render at top level.

## Users

- **Producer / operator using the Herdr worklist** — browses the top-level selection list to choose what to work on next.
  - *As a producer, I want the top-level list to contain only root work items, so I am not shown the same unit of work twice and the list stays short enough to scan.*
- **Developer/agent triaging critical work** — needs release-blocking critical work to remain discoverable.
  - *As a triager, I want a critical child to be reachable from the top level via its parent, so hiding the duplicate row does not make the work invisible.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Top-level invariant**: the default Herdr worklist contains **no** item with a non-empty `parentId`, critical items included. Enforced on the merged set (browse feed + all mandatory subsets) for **both** fetch paths — the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle path (`assembleDefaultWorklist`) and the per-subset fallback — and by removing the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` exception from the root filter in `selectWorkItems`.
2. **Parent substitution preserves reachability**: when a critical child is dropped from the top level, its **root ancestor** (walking the `parentId` chain to the top-most non-child item) is included instead whenever that root is not already in the selected set. The substituted root joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`) and is sorted by its own priority/group. No badge, marker, or indicator is added to the substituted row.
3. **No regression for existing behaviour**:
   - non-critical children remain hidden from the top level exactly as today;
   - drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children);
   - stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with **no** synthetic/substituted rows;
   - the CLI is unchanged for other consumers: `wl list --priority critical` still returns children (the ship critical-items gate must keep seeing them) and `wl worklist`'s `critical` subset keeps its current all-parent-levels query.
4. **Testing & validation**: unit tests cover the removed critical exception, the substitution rule (root ancestor promotion, parent already visible → no duplicate, parent in a non-critical group, count/mandatory interaction), and both fetch paths; the previously added critical-exception tests are updated/inverted. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
5. **Documentation**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. At minimum: the root-filter comment in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, the critical-subset note in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/worklist.ts`, and the Herdr worklist section of `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **No new hot-path `wl` spawn.** Root-ancestor resolution must use the existing in-process SQLite fast path first (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`), with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback. The refresh-spawn budget work (WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) must not regress.
- **No data mutation.** Substitution is display-layer only: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage`.
- **Keep the `wl worklist` critical subset query as-is** (all parent levels, one spawn). It doubles as the discovery feed that tells the Herdr layer which parents to surface; making it root-only would require a second query per refresh.
- **Ship-gate semantics untouched.** `wl list --priority critical --status open` (exit code 7 gate) and the downtime critical candidate path keep their current child-inclusive behaviour.
- Fail-open: if a parent cannot be resolved (missing/deleted), the child is simply not shown at top level — never crash the refresh, never fall back to rendering the child at top level.

## Existing state

- **Why the duplicate exists today.** Commit `cae8ea8a` ("fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list") deliberately reintroduced critical children into the top level: the critical subset query dropped `--root-only` and `selectWorkItems` gained the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception. Rationale: child criticals (e.g. untriaged `[test-failure]` items) were invisible in the worklist while the ship critical-items gate still blocked release on them (exit code 7).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` root filter: `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId || i.priority === 'critical')`; `isMandatoryItem` treats any critical item as mandatory.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — `WORKLIST_LIST_SUBSET_QUERIES.critical = { priority: 'critical', status: ['open','in-progress','blocked','completed'] }` with **no** `rootOnly`, documented as "all parent levels: a critical child is as urgent as a critical root". `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots` are all `rootOnly: true`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchMandatorySubsets` issues `wl list --priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (no `--root-only`); `assembleDefaultWorklist` merges bundle subsets with the browse feed then calls `selectWorkItems` + `regroupWorkItems`; the per-subset fallback mirrors this. `fetchItemsByStage` / `fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`.
- `wl worklist` is consumed only by `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (verified by search), so its payload shape is effectively a Herdr-internal contract.
- Current data: 174 critical items, 78 of them children — 77 of those are themselves `completed`/`done` (already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule in `selectWorkItems`), leaving **one** live duplicate: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension has no critical-subset or smart-selection code (removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so no Pi-side change is needed.
- Parent rows already carry `childCount` (rendered as a `Children: N` metadata row and an expand icon), so a substituted parent is discoverable as a container.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`** — root filter becomes `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId)` (no critical exception). Update the doc comment to state the invariant and the substitution contract.
2. **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — add a display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback:
   - partition the critical subset into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level);
   - for each critical child, resolve its root ancestor by walking `parentId` upward;
   - for each resolved root not already present in the merged candidate set, add it to the **mandatory** set (so `browseItemCount` cannot cut it) before `selectWorkItems` runs;
   - resolve parents in-process first (`db.get` via the refresh scope / `withInProcessDb`), falling back to `wl show`; unresolvable parents are skipped (fail-open).
3. **`src/commands/worklist.ts`** — documentation-only update: state that the `critical` subset is intentionally all-parent-levels (discovery feed) and that the top-level-only invariant is enforced by the Herdr consumer.
4. **Tests** — invert/extend `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` (child critical hidden; non-critical children still hidden) and add fetcher-level coverage for both paths in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` plus the per-subset fallback tests.
5. **Docs** — update `packages/herdr/README.md` (worklist/selection behaviour) and the affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — remove the critical exception from the root filter; document the invariant and substitution contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `assembleDefaultWorklist` + per-subset fallback: critical-child partition, root-ancestor resolution, mandatory-set injection; in-process-first parent lookup with `wl show` fail-open fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — invert the "shows child critical items at the top level" case; keep/extend non-critical child cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — bundle path: child critical not rendered at top level; parent substituted and mandatory.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` (per-subset fallback coverage, whichever file currently exercises `fetchNextItems` without the bundle) — same assertions on the fallback path.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — comment/documentation update for the `critical` subset (no behaviour change).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — selection-list behaviour documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — *Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr)* (completed). Introduced the root-only invariant; its critical-related behaviour was later superseded by commit `cae8ea8a`. This item restores the invariant for critical items while keeping reachability via parent substitution.
- **commit `cae8ea8a`** — "fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list" (no work-item reference in the commit message): the deliberate exception this item reverses. Its motivation — critical children flagged by the ship gate being invisible — is preserved through AC2.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — *wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually* (completed): precedent for "represented by parent".
- **WL-0MQI1SX4W0018V9O** — *Child work items appear in Pi TUI selection list when they should be hidden (represented by parent)* (completed): same precedent, Pi side.
- **WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B** — *Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount* (completed): defines the mandatory subsets whose "always shown" rule AC2 preserves for substituted parents.
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** — *Bubble up critical items* (completed): created the dedicated "Critical" group that sits first in the grouped output. Relevant because a substituted parent is **not** critical by priority, so it will not land in that group (see Risks).
- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR** — *Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced* (completed): related priority-inheritance behaviour for critical children.
- **WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE** — mandatory in-progress-root and blocked-root subsets: the sibling subsets that already use `--root-only`.
- **WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** — spawn-budget work governing the consolidated `wl worklist` read and in-process refresh scope that the substitution must reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost top-level visibility (accepted, mitigated).** Hiding critical children means an operator scanning only the top level no longer sees them directly; the ship critical-items gate can still block a release on a child. Mitigation: AC2 surfaces the root ancestor so the work stays reachable; the parent must be expanded to see the child itself.
- **Substituted parent is not marked critical** (operator decision Q3 = no indicator). It joins the mandatory set and is sorted by its own priority/group, so it may sit in a non-critical section. Risk: the release-blocking signal is less prominent. Accepted; revisit as a separate item if it proves insufficient.
- **Parent resolution cost.** Only critical children trigger a lookup, and only when the root is absent from the merged set (currently one such item). In-process read first; `wl show` is the rare fallback. A per-refresh memo should avoid repeat lookups within a tick.
- **Ancestor promotion depth.** A critical grandchild promotes its **top-most** ancestor, keeping the "no child at top level" invariant. Assumption: promoting the root (not the immediate parent) is correct because the top level may only contain roots.
- **Stage/priority-filtered views are exempt from substitution.** They are explicit filters ("every open item in this stage") and already root-only; injecting a synthetic parent row would misrepresent the filter. Accepted assumption: the ship-gate reachability requirement applies to the default worklist.
- **`wl worklist` payload keeps children in the `critical` subset.** Documented as the discovery feed; a future consumer reading the payload directly would still see children. Accepted, documented in `src/commands/worklist.ts`.
- **Scope creep.** No changes to grouping rules, detail views, badges, or the Pi TUI. Any follow-up (e.g. a critical-child indicator on parents) becomes a separate work item.
- **Assumption**: `parentId` is always present in the payloads used (`wl list`, `wl next`, `wl worklist`) — already relied upon by the existing root-only filters.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** – Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (completed)
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** – Bubble up critical items (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed) — *keyword-only match, unrelated*

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: another, appear, child, children, critical, extension, herdr, level, list, selection, should, show, they, top
- `CLI.md` — matched: same keywords
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: same keywords

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (intake round 1): "What should happen to a critical child whose parent is *not* otherwise in the top-level list (e.g. parent is `done`, or filtered out by the current stage/priority view)? (a) hide it entirely, (b) substitute the parent — show the parent row instead, (c) fallback exception — hide when the parent is visible, show the child when the parent is not, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. B"** — substitute the parent; the child is never rendered at top level.
- **Q2** (intake round 1): "Which lists should the fix cover? (a) default Herdr worklist only, (b) all Herdr top-level lists — default worklist, stage-filtered, priority-filtered, plus both fetch paths, (c) (b) plus CLI semantics, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. B"** — all Herdr top-level lists and both fetch paths; CLI `wl list`/ship-gate semantics unchanged.
- **Q3** (intake round 1): "Should a parent row show a 'critical child' indicator (badge/count) when it is surfaced because of a critical child?" — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "3. no"** — no indicator.
- **Derived assumptions (no question asked)**: (i) a critical child promotes its **top-most** ancestor, because the top level may only contain roots; (ii) stage/priority-filtered views get no substitution — they are explicit filters and already root-only; (iii) the substituted parent keeps its own priority/group (no critical marking, per Q3); (iv) an unresolvable parent means the child is simply not shown (fail-open).
- **Research note**: verified via `wl worklist --json` that the `critical` subset is the only mandatory subset without `rootOnly` (174 items, 78 children; 77 of those are `completed`/`done` and already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule, leaving one live duplicate `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` under `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`). Traced the deliberate exception to commit `cae8ea8a` (no work-item reference) which removed `--root-only` from the critical query and added the `priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception to keep ship-gate-flagged child criticals visible. Confirmed `wl worklist` has a single consumer (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) and that `fetchItemsByStage`/`fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`. Confirmed the Pi TUI has no critical-subset/smart-selection code.

# Extract worklist constants, types and layout

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 1 of 7 extraction slices (leaf modules).

## Target outcome

The three leaf modules of the split exist, carry the module-level doc comments
required by parent AC6, and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports them from
its barrel position — no consumer or test change required.

## Scope (measured line ranges on the current `dev` tree)

| New module | Contents (current `worklist.ts` lines) | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.constants.ts` | Constants (164–224): `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`/`Stage`, `STAGE_MAP`, `PRIORITY_MAP`, `STAGE_COLORS`; `ANSI` (345–368); mouse timing `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` (3558–3592); any tooltip/chord tuning constants | ~170 |
| `worklist.types.ts` | `TermSize`, `ViewMode`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `DisplayRow`, `NavigationStackEntry`, `HelpIconRow`, `KeyAction`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`, `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`, `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution` | ~420 |
| `worklist.layout.ts` | `MIN_META_SHARE`, `MAX_META_SHARE`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`, `computeDynamicLayout` (226–316), `getTermSize` (327–344) | ~130 |

`worklist.types.ts` **must be a leaf**: type-only declarations, no imports from
any other `worklist.*` module (parent AC4 — this is what keeps later modules
cycle-free).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `worklist.constants.ts`, `worklist.types.ts` and `worklist.layout.ts` exist,
   each ≤1,000 lines, each opening with a doc comment stating its single
   responsibility (AC6).
2. Provenance comments move with their code: the `// ── Constants ──`,
   `// ── /wl <stage> argument map (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) ──`,
   `// ── /wl --priority <priority> map (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ──`,
   `// ── Metadata panel sizing ──`, `// ── Terminal helpers ──` banners and all
   inline work-item ids survive verbatim in the destination modules.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports the symbols in this slice that
   consumers actually use — `ANSI`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, `STAGES`, `Stage`,
   `TermSize`, `getTermSize`, `computeMetadataPanelHeight`,
   `computeDynamicLayout`, `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`,
   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by
   the barrel, because no external consumer imports them): `KeyAction`,
   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still
   exported from `./worklist.js`, no worklist module imports the barrel at
   runtime, no new cycle, all modules ≤1,000 lines (AC4, AC1, AC2).
5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full
   `packages/herdr` suite passes with **no test-file changes** (AC3, AC9).
6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:
   `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block around line 2345 and the
   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).
7. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
   → Owned by this slice: no test file is modified and the `packages/herdr` suite is green.
8. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
   → Owned by this slice: the guard's cycle gate reports no new circular import.
9. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
   → Owned by this slice: each module created here carries a responsibility doc comment and the moved provenance banners/comments are verbatim.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `worklist.types.ts`; move the type declarations only (no behaviour).

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — module layout / symbol references.
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` — `formatItemLine` module reference.

## Constraints

- Move-only: no renames, no logic edits, no new formatting of moved code.
- No test file edits (`worklist*.test.ts` stay byte-identical).
- No imports from `./worklist.js` or `index.ts` inside the new modules.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).

## Deliverables

Three leaf modules + barrel re-exports + docs reference updates, all green.

production module (parent AC5) and the gated-tick/input-active predicate beside
