# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-input.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-render.ts` — new (holds the orchestrator).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — re-exports `runWorklistTui`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — consumer; must compile unchanged.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` and the five `docs/dev/*` files listed above.

## Constraints

- No class-based controller conversion, no state duplication, no reordering of
  lifecycle steps, no changed defaults or timings.
- The context is interface-typed and passed explicitly; closures may become
  module functions but must not change observable behaviour.
- No barrel/`index.ts` imports inside the new modules; no test edits.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).
- `WL-0MVND6DHH008R3LG` — constants/types/layout.
- `WL-0MVND6F9V004IQ3V` — state/navigation.
- `WL-0MVND6H5Q006YO9Z` — presentation.
- `WL-0MVND6J090041GWK` — input pipeline (key/mouse handlers move with it).
- `WL-0MVND6KVF0089878` — renderer/commands (the loop dispatches through them).

## Deliverables

Five TUI modules with a thin `runWorklistTui`, guard + full suite green, docs
updated.

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

ACs:
- [ ] Reproduce the failure deterministically (unit test or scripted proxy stub) for a prompt above 38k warm and above 25k cold, recording the observed proxy response headers.
- [ ] Document the confirmed thresholds and the refusal semantics (hard error vs fallback) in docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md.
- [ ] A local-only request over the ceiling produces a deterministic, observable outcome - no silent stall - with the reason recorded in .worklog/local-route.log.
- [ ] The chosen mitigation (fallback, hard error, or pre-dispatch routing) is covered by tests on both sides of each threshold.
- [ ] Operators can see over-threshold refusals without reading raw JSONL (documented query/ or herdr view).
- [ ] Full test suite green.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.
data.title: tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

## Goal

Extract the dependency-free foundation of `SqlitePersistentStore` — the interface set, the SQL-binding/escaping utilities and the in-memory query cache — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` behind the unchanged `persistent-store.ts` façade, so that every later module can import stable siblings without importing the façade.

This is the first **vertical slice**: new modules + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs evidence in one deliverable commit series.

## Scope

Three new modules plus the barrel/delegation wiring:

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/types.ts` — extracted interfaces **and** the internal `StoreContext` type (the injected handle for `db`, cache options/map, fts flag and read-only flag).

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/cache.ts` — cache get/set/invalidate helpers and the mutation-scoped invalidators.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/types.ts` contains `MigrationInfo`, `PersistentStoreServices`, `FtsSearchResult`, `PersistentStoreOpenOptions`, `LastExportTimestamps`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`, `DbMetadata`, `RequiredColumn`, `CacheEntry` and the internal `StoreContext` type, moved **verbatim** (same fields, optionality, JSDoc). The file carries a header comment stating its single responsibility.

## Goal

Extract the work-item persistence concern — the 24-column upsert, lookups, counts, duplicate detection, sort-index batching, hierarchy ordering and `rowToWorkItem` mapping — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/work-items.ts`, the largest and riskiest slice after FTS.

Fourth vertical slice: module + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs in one deliverable.

## Scope

`persistent-store/work-items.ts` — `saveWorkItem`, `getWorkItem`, `countWorkItems`, `getRecentDuplicateByNormalizedTitle`, `escapeLikePattern`, `getAllWorkItems`, `batchUpdateSortIndices`, `getAllWorkItemsOrderedByHierarchySortIndex`, `getAllWorkItemsOrderedByHierarchySortIndexSkipCompleted`, `orderItemsByHierarchySortIndexSkipCompleted`, `deleteWorkItem`, `clearWorkItems`, `rowToWorkItem`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/work-items.ts` contains every method listed in Scope, moved verbatim — the 24-column upsert SQL, its parameter ordering, the `null` normalisation calls, the `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` clause, the hierarchy-ordering comparators and every `ORDER BY` are byte-identical to the pre-move code. The file carries a responsibility header comment.
2. `saveWorkItem` keeps its exact behaviour: same column list, same `normalizeSqliteValue`/`normalizeSqliteBindings` usage, same cache invalidation call, same audit/status normalisation order.
3. Hierarchy ordering is unchanged: `getAllWorkItemsOrderedByHierarchySortIndex`, the skip-completed variants and `orderItemsByHierarchySortIndexSkipCompleted` return the same order for the same rows (asserted by the existing `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` suite, untouched).
4. `rowToWorkItem` moves unchanged (identical column→field mapping, identical fallbacks/coercions) and is not duplicated in the façade.
5. Cache invalidation is preserved: the work-item invalidator is still called on save, delete and clear, using the invalidators from `cache.ts` — no key family dropped (guarded by `dirty-tracking.test.ts`).
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green; the new module stays ≤ 1000 lines (current estimate ~560, comfortably inside).
7. Move-only: no SQL, ordering, error-message or public-signature change; no existing test file modified.
8. `npm run build:shared` and the changed-scope test gate (test skill) pass — `database.test.ts`, `dirty-tracking.test.ts` and `database-dedup.test.ts` in particular.
9. `packages/shared/README.md` Package Structure lists `work-items.ts` with its single responsibility.

## Minimal implementation

1. Inventory `this.` accesses per method (`this.db`, `this._cache*`, `this.cacheGet/Set`, `this.invalidate*`) and express them on the `StoreContext` created in the foundation child.
2. Cut the methods into module-level functions over the context; keep class methods as one-line delegates (`return workItems.saveWorkItem(ctx, item)` or an equivalent named-export style) so the public signatures stay identical.
3. Move `rowToWorkItem` with the same file so mappers live beside their own row shape.
4. Prove the move with a mechanical diff: extract the moved line ranges from the pre-move file (`git show HEAD:packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`) and diff them against the new module, ignoring the `this.` → `ctx.` prefix change.

## Constraints

- Move-only; the 24-column upsert is the single highest drift risk in this item — no reformatting of that SQL, no column reordering.
- Do not change sort-index semantics, gap handling or duplicate-detection windows.
- Do not fold `rowToComment`/`rowToDependencyEdge` in here (they belong to the next child).

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/work-items.ts` — new.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/{types,cache,sql-bindings}.ts` — import sources.
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts`, `.../dirty-tracking.test.ts`, `.../database-dedup.test.ts` — must pass untouched.
- `packages/shared/README.md`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the schema/metadata child (context and cache modules must be settled first).

## Deliverables

- `work-items.ts` + façade delegation, existing suite untouched and green.
- README entry, commit(s) recorded on this item.

4. The transaction helpers keep identical semantics (`BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` behaviour, immediate variant, nesting/re-entrancy behaviour as today) and remain reachable from the façade with unchanged visibility.

## Goal

Seventh vertical slice, and the one most likely to need a genuine collaborator seam: `fts.ts` must reach work-item/comment rows through the injected `StoreContext`, never through the façade.

## Scope

`persistent-store/fts.ts` — `initializeFts`, `upsertFtsEntry`, `deleteFtsEntry`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, `searchFts`, `searchFallback`, `countOccurrences`, `generateSnippet`, `findByIdSubstring`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/fts.ts` contains the full FTS surface listed in Scope, moved verbatim — identical `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE`/trigger DDL, identical ranking (`bm25` weights), identical snippet markers and lengths, identical fallback scoring. The file carries a responsibility header comment.
2. Search ranking and result shape are unchanged: `searchFts` returns the same `FtsSearchResult[]` field set and ordering for the same data, and `searchFallback` produces the same matched-field/snippet/score output as today (guarded by `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` and the CLI search suites, untouched).
3. FTS availability probing and rebuild are unchanged: `initializeFts`/`detectFtsAvailable` keep the same probe and the same "no FTS5 available" degradation path, including `ftsAvailable` getter behaviour on the façade.
4. `rebuildFtsIndex` keeps its single-pass rebuild semantics and returned `{ indexed }` count, and still reads rows through the context rather than an import of the façade.
5. `findByIdSubstring` and the snippet helpers keep identical behaviour, including case handling and `maxLen` truncation.
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green; `fts.ts` ≤ 1000 lines (current estimate ~470).
7. No module under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` imports `./persistent-store.js`; the guard suite's static import scan passes.

2. Cut the methods into `fts.ts` as context-taking functions; keep class delegates so signatures stay identical.
3. Keep the FTS cache invalidation and the `ftsAvailable` flag updates in the same positions relative to writes.

## Constraints

- Move-only; ranking, snippet and fallback behaviour are user-visible in the `wl search` output, so no "while we're here" tuning.

Blocked by the audit-results child (all relational modules must be in place before the search layer moves).

11. Serialisation check performed: the sibling `WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT`

# Extract search, sync and import-export modules and close out

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — decompose `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
**Type:** task (move-only extraction + closeout)
**Position in chain:** 7 of 7 — final verification and docs.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the remaining concerns (FTS/semantic search, Git/JSONL
sync, JSONL import/export) out of the god class, the public API proven
byte-compatible, the docs re-pointed, and the 1,000-line ceiling verified by
machine and by hand — leaving `database.ts` as a thin façade.

Remaining concerns of the god class, ~790 combined lines:

- `database/search.ts` — `search`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, semantic-index
  create/trigger/remove (~210 lines). `docs/dev/fts.md` names

   exist; the methods listed in Context live in exactly one of them as pure
   functions over the shared context, and `database.ts` keeps only thin
   delegating members with identical signatures.

   constructor), plus `WorklogDatabaseServices`, `JsonlImportResult`,

   module that every extracted module may import — asserted by the slice-1
   guard test.
6. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package

`.pi/test-config.json` pins `suiteCommands` to `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` and `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. `run_tests.py changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` when custom suite commands are declared, so the implement finish gate and the pre-push full-scope hook only execute those two directories.

Colocated extension suites (`packages/tui/extensions/**/*.test.ts` — e.g. `Worklog/session-health.test.ts`, `Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.test.ts`) therefore never run in the local gate; they only run in CI (`.github/workflows/cli-tests.yml` → `npm test`). The gap is pre-existing (not introduced by WL-0MVGB23MM004X501), but it means extension-only regressions cannot be caught locally.

## Scope

- Decide whether to add a third suite command for `packages/tui/extensions` (and/or `packages/herdr`, which already has a group), weighing runtime cost.
- If added, verify `run_tests.py --scope full --summary` still records a single full-suite cache entry that audits accept.

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 22 + shared 12 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 22 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 12 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **440** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (22 files, incl. `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (12 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any `groups.*` entry, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them.

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — extend the shared "Test gates" section + coverage table

# Audit fingerprint parity skew must never be silent (test + doctor)

Discovered-from: LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM (false-stale audit badge, 2026-10-25).

## Problem statement

`wl list` / `wl worklist` / review-queue grouping compute a *current* audit
content fingerprint with the TypeScript port (`src/audit-fingerprint.ts`,
**schema 2** since WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7 / commit `213a96b7`, 2026-10-23) and
compare it against the *stored* fingerprint persisted by the audit skill's
Python implementation (installed at `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts`,
sourced from SorraAgents `skill/audit`).

When the two sides compute **different payloads** (a `schema` key,
git-derived `path_states`, extra hash inputs), the digests can never match.
`isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts:457`) short-circuits on
`storedFingerprint === currentFingerprint` and returns false. Every audit
persisted under such a skew therefore renders as **out-of-date / stale** in
every `isAuditFresh`-driven view, even when the audit is genuinely current
and "Ready to close: Yes".

Observed on LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM: the stored fingerprint reproduced exactly
with the *then-installed* Python skill (pre-v2 formula
`{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`), yet `wl list` reported a
different `currentFingerprint` → the item showed as needing re-audit.

This skew is **silent** by design: `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts`
classifies any schema mismatch ("ahead or behind") as a **skip** that names the
installed schema — so the drift ships green and no-one is told that audit
freshness is broken end-to-end.

## Users

- **Worklog/agent operators** relying on audit freshness flags to know which
  `in_review` items truly need re-auditing; a false-stale flag wastes a
  re-audit and erodes trust in the queue.
- **Release-gate consumers** (`wl doctor audit-gaps`, review queue) that
  classify items via `isAuditFresh` / `assessAuditInvalidate`.

**User story:** "As a worklog operator, I want a fingerprint-schema skew
between the installed audit skill and this CLI to fail a test (or at minimum
surface as a `wl doctor` warning), so the false-stale audit badge cannot ship
silently."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `evaluateInstalledContract` no longer treats a schema skew as a silent
  skip. A helper that declares a schema (any number) different from
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` — ahead **or** behind — **fails** the
  parity test with an actionable message naming the installed schema, the
  expected schema, the scripts directory, and the remediation (port schema N
  in the installed skill, or point `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` at one that does).
- AC2: a helper that declares **no schema** at all (pre-v2 install) is treated
  as skew: the test **fails** with a message naming the installed path and
  schema constant lookup, because an undeclared schema cannot be proven
  compatible (fail-safe: never claim parity on unprovable data). A test
  documents exactly the observed failure: a schema-1 Python report's stored
  fingerprint never matches the schema-2 `computeContentFingerprint` for the
  same title/description.
- AC3: genuine *environment unavailability* remains a skip, not a red herring:
  no scripts dir, no `python3`, or an unimportable helper each skip with the
  existing descriptive reason (CI images without the agent framework stay
  green).
- AC4: `wl doctor` gains a warning-level check
  (e.g. `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`) that reports the installed vs
  expected schema and remediation when the installed audit skill's schema
  differs from `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` or is undeclared. The check
  is a warning (non-failing) so existing workflows are not broken, but it
  appears in `wl doctor` output and `--json`.
- AC5: an end-to-end freshness test proves the reported failure mode and its
  fix: an item whose stored fingerprint was produced by a schema-2 Python
  report is `isAuditFresh`; a schema-1-report fingerprint (or a schema-1-style
  current computation) is not. The test is self-contained (in-memory
  audit-record fixtures) — this repo currently has **zero** fingerprint-bearing
  audits since the 2026-10-23 schema-2 port (verified: all 66 stored
  fingerprints predate it), so live data cannot be relied upon.
- AC6: docs updated: the module docstring in `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`, the
  parity test header, and `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` state the new
  fail-on-skew contract (the old "skip on skew" rationale is removed — the
  table in `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` § "Parity check and host tooling
  skew" still documents skip-on-skew and must be inverted).
- AC7: the full test suite passes with the changes. **No strictness env gate
  is required**: the schema-2 Python side has already shipped (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP
  `completed/done`; installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  declares `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2` at line 1222 and emits the
  schema-2 payload at line 2433, install 2026-10-26 00:50), so fail-on-skew is
  green on this host. Env-unavailability cases (AC3) remain skips.

## Constraints

- **No change to the fingerprint payload itself in this repo** — parity and
  diagnostics only.
- **Strict-by-default contract (operator-confirmed option 1A):** a host with a
  pre-v2 or undeclared-schema installed skill now *fails* the parity test and
  shows the `wl doctor` warning on purpose. This is the intended behaviour —
  the actionable message (AC1/AC2) tells the operator to reinstall the
  framework skills (`cd ~/projects/SorraAgents && git pull && scripts/install_pi.sh`)
  or point `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` at a schema-2 install. A legacy
  `AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_PARITY_STRICT` env gate is **not** added (it would
  re-create the silence this item is meant to end).
- The skip path for missing environments (AC3) must be preserved; CI without
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` or `python3` must not fail.
- The `wl doctor` check (AC4) probes the installed skill the same way the
  parity test does (operator-confirmed option 2A): a `python3` subprocess
  reading `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` and the helper signature, with a
  graceful skip when `python3`, the scripts dir, or the import is unavailable
  (mirrors AC3). One subprocess per `wl doctor` run is acceptable.

## Existing state (verified in repo)

- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2`;
  `computeContentFingerprint` hashes `{schema: 2, title_hash, description_hash}`
  with zero git calls (WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7).
- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — `evaluateInstalledContract`
  returns a skip reason string for skew (`'installed audit skill at … implements
  schema <n> but this repository expects schema <expected>'`) and the unit test
  `'skips with the installed schema when the helper is ahead or behind'`
  (line ~146) asserts the skip. This is the line that must be inverted.
  `findAuditScripts()` / `pythonAvailable()` helpers already exist for the
  env-missing cases (AC3).
- Installed helper: `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` now
  declares `_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA = 2` (line 1222) and computes
  the schema-2 payload via `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2385-2433).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:444` `isAuditFresh` — primary gate is a bare
  string compare; mismatch ⇒ stale; no skew diagnostics (unchanged by this
  item — operator-confirmed option 3A keeps read paths untouched).
- Consumers seen today: `src/commands/grouping.ts:287`, `src/list-enrichment.ts`.
- `wl doctor` findings carry `checkId` / `severity: 'warning'` (e.g.
  `priority.invalid`, `upgrade.pending` in `src/commands/doctor.ts`) — the new
  check slots into that assembly; no doctor schema change needed.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` § "Parity check and host tooling skew" still
  documents the old skip-on-skew policy table (must be inverted per AC6).

## Desired change

1. **Invert the skew policy in the parity test.** `evaluateInstalledContract`
   (and its callers) now *fail* on any declared schema ≠ 2 and on an
   undeclared schema, with an actionable message. Environment-unavailability
   stays a skip (AC3). The two existing skew tests are updated from
   "skips" to "fails" and supplemented with an undeclared-schema case (AC2).
2. **Add a `wl doctor` warning check** `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`
   (AC4) that probes the installed skill and reports installed vs expected
   schema + remediation in both human output and `--json`.
3. **Add a self-contained end-to-end freshness test** (AC5) proving a
   schema-2 stored fingerprint is fresh and a schema-1 one is not.
4. **Update documentation** (AC6) so the fail-on-skew contract is
   authoritative.

## Key Files

- `tests/unit/audit-fingerprint-parity.test.ts` — invert the skew policy;
  add undeclared-schema failure and the AC5 freshness test; keep AC3 skips.
- `src/audit-fingerprint.ts` — docstring update only (fail-on-skew contract);
  payload unchanged.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — register the new warning check in the doctor
  findings assembly (human output + `--json`).
- `src/doctor/audit-fingerprint-skew-check.ts` (new) — installed-skill probe
  (shared shape with the parity test) + warning finding
  `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew`.
- `docs/dev/audit-fingerprint.md` — invert the skew-policy table and
  remediation text.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — reference only; no behavioural change.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7` (completed, bug) — schema-2 TS port; the skip-on-skew
  policy inverted here was introduced there.
- `WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV` (completed, feature) — `audit_results` fingerprint
  column on existing DBs; underpins stored-vs-current comparison: with a NULL
  fingerprint the fallback time gate applies rather than a skew.
- `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` (completed, feature) — central read cache; relevant
  because the new `wl doctor` probe adds a subprocess to that path's tooling.
- `SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP` (completed, SorraAgents, cross-repo) — the hard
  prerequisite; shipped and reinstalled (verified 2026-10-26).
- `LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM` — the observed false-stale audit that motivated this
  item; manual re-verification target after implementation.

See also the automated report appended in § "Related work (automated report)".

## Verification

- Unit: parity-test skew cases (ahead / behind / undeclared) fail with the
  actionable message; env-missing cases still skip; AC5 freshness test
  (schema-2 fresh, schema-1 stale).
- Integration: `wl doctor` on this repo's worklog shows no
  `audit-fingerprint.schema-skew` warning while the installed skill is schema
  2, and shows the warning + remediation when `AUDIT_SKILL_SCRIPTS` is pointed
  at a pre-v2 install (contract unit test).
- Manual: re-audit LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM after implementation and confirm
  `wl list` shows the audit fresh (stored == currentFingerprint).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Strictness of the parity test now the prerequisite (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP)
  has shipped?" — Answer (operator): "continue" — proceeded with the
  recommended option **1A: fail unconditionally on skew/undeclared schema;
  drop the `AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_PARITY_STRICT` gate**. Source: interactive
  reply "continue" to the intake round of 2026-10-27, where the recommendation
  was shown explicitly. Research: verified `audit_runner.py:1222` schema 2,
  SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP `completed/done`.
- Q2: "How should the `wl doctor` check inspect the installed skill?" —
  Answer (operator): "continue" — proceeded with **2A: python3 subprocess
  probe mirroring the parity test; graceful skip on missing python3/scripts/
  import**. Source: interactive reply "continue".
- Q3: "Scope of skew surfacing beyond test + doctor?" — Answer (operator):
  "continue" — proceeded with **3A: parity test + `wl doctor` only;
  `isAuditFresh` / `wl list` unchanged**. Note: a `wl list` skew diagnostic
  (e.g. `fingerprintSkew: true`) was discussed and deliberately **out of
  scope** (recorded as a follow-up opportunity — see Risks). Source:
  interactive reply "continue".
- Research summary: the constraint in the original brief ("installed skill is
  still pre-v2; strict gate required") was found **stale** during intake — the
  installed skill now declares schema 2. This repo has zero fingerprint-bearing
  audits since 2026-10-23 (all 66 stored fingerprints predate the TS port), so
  AC5 must use in-memory fixtures rather than live data.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** a `wl list` skew diagnostic and richer `isAuditFresh`
  mismatch reporting are real opportunities but deliberately excluded (Q3).
  Track via a follow-up work item if the doctor warning proves insufficient.
- **Host-deployment surprise:** after this lands, any host still running a
  pre-v2 installed skill fails the parity test with an actionable message. This
  is the intended contract, but it is a new failure mode for the first run on
  a stale host — mitigated by the message clearly naming the remediation.
- **Assumption:** a single `python3` subprocess per `wl doctor` run is an
  acceptable cost. If doctor latency on this probe ever matters, it can be
  cached (cf. WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3).
- **Assumption:** `evaluateInstalledContract` stays a pure unit-testable
  function; the doctor check re-uses the same probe rather than duplicating
  import logic.
- **Failure mode:** if the installed skill later moves *ahead* of this repo
  (schema 3), the suite fails by design and the operator must decide whether
  to port this repo forward — the message names both schemas so the decision
  is explicit.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVK5SWZE00254Y7** – Host tooling skew: audit-fingerprint-parity fails against the installed global audit skill (completed)
- **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV** – a-y audit approve silently no-ops: audit_results missing fingerprint column on existing databases (completed)

# Refactor guard: sync split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 6 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/sync.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely, no existing test file changes, and no reviewer
has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC1 require an unchanged public surface at `./sync.js`, an
unmodified test suite, an acyclic import graph, and no file above 1,000 lines.
Nothing in the root package enforces any of that today: there is no
`madge`/`dependency-cruiser`, the repo-wide file-size guard
(WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL) is still `idea`, and the only existing split guards are
the `packages/herdr` ones (`downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`,
`index.split-guard.test.ts`) which are scoped to that package. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring the guard child of the sibling
decomposition (WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E for `downtime-worker.ts`) and the
`packages/shared` equivalent (WL-0MVOBOX1U0013HNF).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-26, `dev` @ `f39b2463`-era tree):

- `src/sync.ts` — 1,867 lines, **34 exports = 25 value exports (functions and
  one `const`) + 9 type exports (8 `interface` + 1 `type` alias)**. (The parent
  description's "23 functions/consts + 11 interfaces/types" split is corrected
  here; the total of 34 is unchanged.)
- 10 source files import from `./sync.js` / `../sync.js`: `src/database.ts`,
  `src/logging.ts`, `src/api.ts`, `src/index.ts`,
  `src/commands/{sync,init,migrate,helpers,doctor,delete}.ts`.
- 11 test files import from `../src/sync.js` (two of them via dynamic
  `await import()`): `sync.test.ts`, `sync-whitelist.test.ts`,
  `sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `sync-worktree.test.ts`,
  `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
  `sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`,
  `sync-audit-results.test.ts`, `unit/audit-sync-monotonic.test.ts`,
  `cli/git-mock-roundtrip.test.ts`.
- 1 internal importer: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `type { MergeOptions }`
  from `'../sync.js'` — the only known would-be cycle, to be re-pointed at
  `src/sync/types.ts` by child 2.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure — `src/sync.ts` and every `src/sync*.ts` / `src/sync/**/*.ts` module — is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   Verified mechanically (`wc -l`) and recorded in the completion comment, driven
   by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only `'sync.ts'` and
   is asserted to only ever shrink (remain a subset of the plan-time list).
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The committed baseline `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` records the 34
   symbol names (25 value + 9 type, flagged separately) plus provenance
   (generation command, source commit, timestamp), and a machine gate fails the
   suite when any one is lost — value exports resolvable at runtime, type
   exports present in the emitted declaration.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   The guard's completion evidence shows zero diffs across the 77 existing test
   files; any accidental behavioural delta is reverted, not "fixed" in place.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in the module responsibility table.
   The static import graph of `src/sync.ts` + `src/sync/**/*.ts` contains no
   cycle (no module imports a module that imports it back); after the final child
   no production module under `src/sync/` contains a runtime (value) import of
   `'../sync.js'`. The gate is green now — the single `merge-utils.ts` type-only
   import sits in an explicit allowlist that child 2 removes — and red on any new
   violation.
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
   The guard suite itself is documented the same way, so the standard is
   established before the extraction children land.
6. New **additive** test file `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` (vitest) exists
   and passes on the current tree before any production code moves; no existing
   test file is modified.
7. **Negative proofs.** Each of the three gates is proven to fail on a
   deliberately broken input (synthetic >1,000-line module, dropped export,
   synthetic import cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
8. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes via the test skill, and `npm run build` — for this child, `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes including the
   new guard suite, and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Minimal implementation

1. Generate the baseline from `src/sync.ts` (regex-free, TypeScript compiler
   API or `tsc`-emitted `.d.ts` after `npm run build`) — normalise, sort,
   flag value-vs-type, and write JSON with provenance fields.
2. Write `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` with one named `it()` per gate
   (surface, size + allowlist, cycle/barrel, negative proofs) so failures are
   legible.
3. Put the pure predicates (parse module → imports/exports; build graph; find
   cycles) in `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` so the negative-proof tests can
   feed them synthetic sources without touching the tree.
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and `TYPE_ONLY_BARREL_ALLOWLIST` so child 2 and
   child 6 can shrink them by one line each.
5. Record the baseline generation command in the file header, then run
   `/skill:test` (changed scope) and `npm run build` and paste both outcomes in
   a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — new guard suite.
- `tests/sync/split-guard-scan.ts` — new pure gate predicates/scanners.
- `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` — new frozen export baseline.
- `src/sync.ts` — read-only in this child (no edits).
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — read-only in this child (allowlisted).

## Dependencies

None — first child. Every extraction child (2–6) is blocked by this one.

## Constraints

- Move-only / additive: production code and existing tests are untouched.
- Do not add `madge`, `dependency-cruiser` or any new runtime/dev dependency —
  graph and size checks are plain TypeScript.
- No edits to the `packages/herdr` split guards and no relocation of their
  `scan.ts`; this guard is root-package-scoped. Sharing a common scanner with
  the other packages is deliberately out of scope (would widen blast radius).
- A repo-wide file-size guard remains WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL; this guard covers
  only `sync.ts` and `sync/`.

## Deliverables

Frozen export baseline, guard suite + scanners, negative proofs, green
`/skill:test` (changed scope) and green `npm run build` recorded in a comment.

# Extract author-identity, refs, prefix-filter and repo-context modules

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 4 of 6 — mid-layer; consumes child 2, feeds child 5.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the author-identity gate, the last-synced/remote ref
bookkeeping, the cross-project prefix filter and the repo-root resolution to
each live in a small, individually reviewable module, so identity-gate fixes
are not interleaved with git plumbing.

## Context

Four non-merge concerns occupy the middle of `src/sync.ts`. Current declaration
ranges (plan-time numbering):

- author identity: `normalizeEmail` 371, `isAllowAllAuthors` 376,
  `isEmailWhitelisted` 383, `getRemoteAuthorCommits` 412–449,
  `checkAuthorIdentity` 450–479, `buildIdentityRefusalMessage` 480–502,
  `getConfiguredUserEmail` 503–517, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` 568–596
- refs: `getLastSyncedRefPath` 518, `readLastSyncedRef` 527,
  `writeLastSyncedRef` 539, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha` 552–567,
  `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` 1358, `getRemoteTrackingRef` 1342,
  `fetchRemote` 1338, `refExists` 1360, `fetchTargetRef` 1369–1426
- prefix filter: `isOwnProjectItemId` 287–306, `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` 307–355
- repo context: `getRepoRoot` 1274, `getRepoRootForPath` 1283,
  `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` 1304–1337, `getRepoRelativePath` 1427–1437

Public surface to preserve: `getRemoteAuthorCommits`, `checkAuthorIdentity`,
`getConfiguredUserEmail`, `getLastSyncedRefPath`, `readLastSyncedRef`,
`writeLastSyncedRef`, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`,
`isOwnProjectItemId`, `filterRemoteDataByPrefix`, `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` and
**`_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef`** (consumed by `tests/sync.test.ts` and
`tests/cli/git-mock-roundtrip.test.ts`). All helpers not listed here
(`normalizeEmail`, `isAllowAllAuthors`, `isEmailWhitelisted`,
`buildIdentityRefusalMessage`, `fetchRemote`, `getRemoteTrackingRef`,
`refExists`, `fetchTargetRef`, `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRootForPath`,
`getRepoRelativePath`) are module-local today and stay internal.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. `src/sync/author-identity.ts` holds all eight author-gate functions
   (`normalizeEmail`, `isAllowAllAuthors`, `isEmailWhitelisted`,
   `getRemoteAuthorCommits`, `checkAuthorIdentity`, `buildIdentityRefusalMessage`,
   `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`) moved verbatim, using
   `./git-exec.js` and `./types.js`.
2. `src/sync/refs.ts` holds `getLastSyncedRefPath`, `readLastSyncedRef`,
   `writeLastSyncedRef`, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha`, `getRemoteTrackingRef` and
   the `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` alias; `fetchRemote`, `refExists`,
   `fetchTargetRef` are owned here (module-local) and re-exported for child 5.
3. `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` holds `isOwnProjectItemId` and
   `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` moved verbatim.
4. `src/sync/repo-context.ts` holds `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRootForPath`,
   `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `getRepoRelativePath` moved verbatim.
5. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The barrel re-exports exactly the twelve public symbols of this group and no
   new ones.
6. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts`,
   `tests/sync-whitelist.test.ts` and `tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`
   pass unmodified; `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes and `npm run build`
   succeeds.
7. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic; no module imports a module that imports it back.
   No runtime import of `'../sync.js'` from any `src/sync/` module; the guard
   cycle gate is green.
8. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
9. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   `wc -l` for all touched files is recorded in the completion comment.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create the four new files; move each concern group verbatim with its
   imports (`../process-lifecycle.js`, `../types.js`, `node:*` as originally
   used).
2. Delete the moved blocks from `src/sync.ts`; re-export the twelve public
   symbols from their modules via `export { ... } from './sync/…'`.
3. Build, run `/skill:test` (changed scope), record `wc -l` and both outcomes.

## Key Files

- `src/sync/author-identity.ts` — new. Identity gate, whitelist, refusal message.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — new. Last-synced ref and remote-tracking ref helpers.
- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — new. Cross-project prefix filtering.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — new. Data-file/repo-root resolution and assertion.
- `src/sync.ts` — removes the four groups, keeps re-exports.
- `src/sync/git-exec.ts`, `src/sync/types.ts` — read-only (child 2).

## Dependencies

Blocked by WL-0MVP9PCOU004L8HN (types + git-exec) and WL-0MVP9QLWU003NV41
(merge group). The edge to the merge group is a **landing-order** edge, not a
code dependency — the two groups are code-independent, but both edit the same
`src/sync.ts` surface, so they land serially (parent risk AC: land sequentially
to limit concurrent-change conflicts).

## Constraints

- Move-only: no logic edits, no signature changes, no symbol renames, no new
  dependencies.
- `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` must survive the barrel unchanged.
- No consumer or existing test file edits.
- Land as sequential green commits (refs → repo-context → prefix-filter →
  author-identity).

## Deliverables

Four focused modules, reduced `src/sync.ts`, guard suite green, build +
changed-scope test evidence, `wc -l` table.

# Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 5 of 6 — top of the dependency layer; leaves only the
barrel wiring to child 6.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want temporary-worktree lifecycle, remote content fetch /
delta replay and push (including rewrite-and-force-push) in three separate
modules, so a change to one I/O path is not entangled with the other two.

## Context

Final region of `src/sync.ts`. Current declaration ranges (plan-time
numbering):

- worktree: `removeWorktreeFiles` 1573, `listTrackedFiles` 1580, `ensureDir`
  1586, `withTempWorktree` 1590–1703
- remote: `getRemoteDataFileContentWithRef` 1438–1465,
  `getRemoteDataFileContent` 1466–1472, `replayRemoteDeltaChain` 1510–1572
- push: `gitPushDataFileToBranch` 1704–1797, `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
  1798–1867

`replayRemoteDeltaChain` builds on the worktree helper and the refs helpers from
child 4; push builds on both. The layering is therefore
`worktree → remote → push`, which is acyclic by construction.

Public surface to preserve: `getRemoteDataFileContentWithRef`,
`getRemoteDataFileContent`, `replayRemoteDeltaChain`, `gitPushDataFileToBranch`,
`rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`. `removeWorktreeFiles`, `listTrackedFiles`,
`ensureDir`, `withTempWorktree` stay internal (exported from the module for
internal use only, never from the barrel).

## Acceptance Criteria


1. `src/sync/worktree.ts` holds `removeWorktreeFiles`, `listTrackedFiles`,
   `ensureDir`, `withTempWorktree` moved verbatim, including the existing
   cleanup/`finally` semantics — no behaviour change in the `finally` path.
2. `src/sync/remote.ts` holds `getRemoteDataFileContentWithRef`,
   `getRemoteDataFileContent`, `replayRemoteDeltaChain` moved verbatim, using
   `./worktree.js`, `./refs.js`, `./repo-context.js` and `../jsonl.js`.
3. `src/sync/push.ts` holds `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and
   `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` moved verbatim.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic; no module imports a module that imports it back.
   No lower layer imports a higher one (`worktree` never imports `remote` or
   `push`; `remote` never imports `push`); the guard cycle gate is green.
5. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The barrel re-exports exactly the five public symbols of this group; no
   consumer or test file is edited.
6. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass without modification.
   `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts`, `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` and
   `tests/cli/git-mock-roundtrip.test.ts` pass unmodified; `/skill:test` (changed
   scope) passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
7. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
   `src/sync/worktree.ts`'s header cross-references `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
8. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   `wc -l` for all touched files is recorded in the completion comment.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `src/sync/worktree.ts`; move the four helpers verbatim with their
   `node:fs`/`node:path` imports.
2. Create `src/sync/remote.ts`; move the fetch + replay functions verbatim.
3. Create `src/sync/push.ts`; move the two push functions verbatim.
4. Delete the moved blocks from `src/sync.ts`; re-export the five public
   symbols.
5. Build, run `/skill:test` (changed scope), record `wc -l` and both outcomes.

## Key Files

- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — new. Temporary worktree lifecycle helpers.
- `src/sync/remote.ts` — new. Remote content fetch and delta-replay chain.
- `src/sync/push.ts` — new. Data-file push and force-push/rewrite.
- `src/sync/refs.ts`, `src/sync/repo-context.ts`, `src/sync/git-exec.ts`,
  `src/sync/types.ts` — read-only inputs from children 2 and 4.
- `src/jsonl.ts` — read-only; `replayRemoteDeltaChain` parses via this existing module.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — read-only reference.

## Dependencies

Blocked by WL-0MVP9R3PU004EGYE (refs / repo-context / identity / prefix) —
`replayRemoteDeltaChain` and the push paths call the ref and repo-context
helpers, and this child must not re-create them.

## Constraints

- Move-only: no logic edits, no signature changes, no symbol renames, no new
  dependencies.
- Known awkwardness in this region (duplicated worktree/push preamble,
  recorded in the parent's Risks) must be **recorded as a new work item**, not
  refactored here.
- No consumer or existing test file edits.
- Land as sequential green commits (worktree → remote → push).

## Deliverables

Three focused modules, `src/sync.ts` reduced to the not-yet-barrelled remainder,
guard suite green, build + changed-scope test evidence, `wc -l` table.

# Finalise sync barrel, documentation and close-out

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — decompose `src/sync.ts` god class
**Type:** task
**Position in chain:** 6 of 6 — last; converts `src/sync.ts` into the thin
barrel and lands the docs.

## Goal

As a new contributor, I want `src/sync.ts` to be a thin, readable barrel whose
header explains where each concern lives, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` to map the
new layout — so the decomposition is self-documenting and the maintainability
ceiling is mechanically verified.

## Context

After children 2–5, every function/type has moved out; what remains in
`src/sync.ts` is the barrel re-exports plus any inter-module wiring that was
kept in place. This child removes the last rest-of-file body, or reduces it to
a genuinely-thin barrel, and completes the verification loop for the parent's
seven ACs.

## Acceptance Criteria


1. `src/sync.ts` is a barrel (re-exports plus a documentation header). Every
   production symbol is re-exported exactly once; no consumer or test file
   changes its import path.
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable from `'./sync.js'`.
   The guard suite is green with both allowlists empty.
3. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure is ≤ 1,000 lines.
   `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is reduced to exactly `[]`; `wc -l` for every `src/sync*.ts`
   file is recorded in the completion comment.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in the module responsibility table.
   No module under `src/sync/` imports `'../sync.js'` at runtime and the whole
   `sync*` family graph is acyclic per the guard gate.
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
6. **Documentation updated.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the new module layout — the module

Blocked by WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 (worktree/remote/push) and transitively by all

**Repository:** SorraAgents. Run `implement.py start` with cwd
`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`; `wl` resolves the `WL-` store from the
ContextHub prefix.

**Parent:** WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG (parent AC2, test-first half)

## Goal

As a maintainer I want an automated test that fails when a command run inside
`.worklog/worktrees/<wl-…>` deletes or modifies tracked files in the **main
checkout**, so the "worktree-scoped run mutated the shared checkout" defect
class can never regress silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent criterion AC2 (restated):** **Regression test.** An automated test fails if a command run inside a `.worklog/worktrees/<wl-…>` worktree deletes or modifies tracked files in the main checkout — reproducing the "main checkout mutated by a worktree-scoped run" defect class (the same invariant as [docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](../../docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)).
- [ ] `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` gains tests proving that a
      snapshot/diff pair covering **both** the guarded root and its main
      checkout reports `changed == true` when only the main checkout lost a
      tracked file, and names that path in `describe_diff` output.
- [ ] `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` gains an end-to-end test that
      runs a guarded scope from inside a temporary linked worktree whose child
      process deletes a tracked file in the main checkout, asserting the run
      fails and the message names the mutated path. Until the fix lands this
      test is pinned with `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG")`.
- [ ] A characterisation test pins that finish's own Step 5 fast-forward in the
      main checkout is **expected** churn (never a guard failure), so the fix
      cannot over-block legitimate behaviour.
- [ ] The wheel-stays-green rule holds: the touched test modules pass as
      committed (strict xfail counts as pass, and its removal in the sibling
      fix child is the deliberate flip).
- [ ] Every assertion checks the diagnostic text (path named), not only the
      exit status, so a failure is actionable.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend the `git_sandbox` fixtures to build a repo with a linked worktree and
   a tracked file that the "offending" child process deletes in the main root.
2. Add the xfail-pinned guarded-run test, following the existing

3. Add the fast-forward allow-list characterisation test.

## Goal

As an implementing agent I want `implement.py finish` to abort with a clear
error naming the paths and the concurrent actor when it observes tracked-file
deletions in the main checkout that it did not make, so a silent wipe is never
followed by a `git commit -a` that reverts a whole package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent criterion AC3 (restated):** **Failure is loud.** Any agent step that observes tracked-file deletions in the main checkout while it was not the actor aborts with a clear error naming the paths and the actor, instead of continuing silently.
- [ ] `phase_finish` snapshots the main checkout at run start and re-verifies it
      before the push step and before worktree removal; tracked-file deletions or
      modifications not attributable to finish's own fast-forward abort the run
      with every offending path listed.
- [ ] The abort message names the concurrent actor evidence available at runtime
      (worktree process registry entry, PID, session id, or "unknown") and the
      recovery command (`git checkout -- <path>`), and the work item is left
      `open` (never `completed`/`in_review`).
- [ ] Finish's own Step 5 fast-forward churn is classified as expected and never
      aborts; a clean run is unaffected and the existing
      `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` stays green.
- [ ] `report["steps"]["main_checkout_guard"]` records the snapshot time, verify
      times and the verdict, so an operator can read the guard's work from the
      finish report (observability).
- [ ] New tests in `skill/implement/tests/` cover: foreign deletion aborts with
      the path named, own fast-forward does not abort, and a clean finish
      reports the guard step as passing.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Reuse `_main_checkout_offending_paths` plus the finish report plumbing
   (it already computes non-`.worklog/` dirty paths and is used by the
   placement gates).
2. Add snapshot/verify calls around Steps 4-7 and a `_classify_own_churn`
   allow-list for the fast-forward.

# Single-owner lock for the main checkout during finish

**Repository:** SorraAgents. Run `implement.py start` with cwd
`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`; `wl` resolves the `WL-` store from the
ContextHub prefix.

**Parent:** WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG (parent AC5)

## Goal

As a maintainer I want two `implement.py finish` runs to be unable to operate on
the same main checkout at the same time, so the 2026-10-26 overlap (two finishes
plus a full-scope test run on one shared checkout) is refused up front with a
named holder instead of corrupting the working tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Parent criterion AC5 (restated):** **Concurrent-run detection.** `implement.py finish` refuses to start, or warns explicitly, when another agent process holds the main checkout on the same host (see also `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`).
- [ ] `implement.py finish` takes an exclusive advisory lock on
      `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock` before the commit step
      and releases it on every exit path (success, error, abort).
- [ ] A second finish against the same main checkout exits non-zero with a
      message naming the holder (work item id, PID, start time recorded in the
      lock file) and does not modify the checkout or the work item.
- [ ] No stale locks are possible: a killed holder is released by the kernel
      (flock), proven by a test that SIGKILLs the holder and re-acquires.
- [ ] Finishes in **different** repositories on the same host are unaffected
      (per-checkout scope), proven by a test.
- [ ] `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports a held lock and any tracked-file
      deletions in the main checkout in both human and `--json` output, reusing
      its existing dirty-checkout detection.
- [ ] Tests cover contention, crash release, cross-checkout independence and the
      hygiene script output; the lock adds no measurable finish latency (single
      non-blocking acquire, recorded in `report["steps"]`).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Reuse the flock slot pattern from `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`
   (kernel-released locks, no PID bookkeeping to trust).
2. Write holder metadata (work item id, PID, ISO start time, repo root) into the
   lock file after acquisition, for the refusal message only.
3. Wrap the finish critical section and add the report entry.
4. Extend `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` with lock + deletion reporting.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` critical section.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — reusable flock pattern.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — new tests.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — lock and deletion reporting.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — concurrency contract note.

**Dependencies:** the finish-abort child (same function; serialising avoids
conflicting edits).
**Deliverables:** lock, refusal message, tests, hygiene reporting, docs.

## Problem

The test-run cache (`skill/test_cache.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

**Implementation repository:** the cache code lives in the **SorraAgents** skills repo. This item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog (where it was discovered); all paths below are relative to the SorraAgents repo root.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `run_cached()`, `lookup()`, `store()`, `query_cached()`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `--scope changed`, `--summary`, `[cached]` marker in non-JSON output
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — existing cache-fingerprint unit tests
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — existing run_tests cache-integration tests
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — the test-skill cache contract documentation

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Verified context (checked while planning, 2026-10-30)

- **Content-sensitive fingerprinting already shipped.** SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (commit `b51609654`, 2026-10-20) made `compute_git_state()` hash HEAD **plus the content of every path** in `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`. Symptom 1 was observed on 2026-10-26, *after* that fix — so the residual stale hit is **not** the already-fixed content-hash gap; the implementer must reproduce it and find the path that bypasses or mis-times the fingerprint.
- **Symptom 2 has an identified mechanism.** `run_cached()` computes `git_state` **before** the run and stores the entry under that pre-run state, so any transient dirty state at run start (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) keys an entry that a clean checkout at the same HEAD can never query again.
- **The `[cached]` marker already exists** in non-JSON run output (SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY, 2026-08-06), so cache visibility is a regression-guard requirement rather than new behaviour.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Content-only edits invalidate: editing only the contents of an already-modified (dirty) file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group, proven by a regression test (run A → edit an already-dirty file → run B) that fails against the un-fixed code and passes after the fix.
- AC2 — Post-run queryability: immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full` completes, `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` from a clean checkout at the same HEAD reports the stored entry instead of `missing`, covered by a regression test.
- AC3 — Cache visibility guarded: a cache-served result remains marked `[cached]` in non-JSON output and that marker is covered by a regression test so it cannot silently regress.
- AC4 — Root cause recorded: the mechanism behind each symptom is recorded on this item as a comment before the fix lands, and both regression tests are demonstrated RED against the pre-fix code and GREEN afterwards.
- AC5 — Docs: `skill/test/SKILL.md` states that runs whose result proves RED/GREEN (or supplies evidence an audit consumes) must use `--no-cache`.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Changing the cache key/namespace model (tree fingerprints, worktree/main-checkout unification) — tracked by SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB and SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V. This item must not duplicate or block those.

## Risky assumptions

- The residual stale hit (symptom 1) is fixable without changing the fingerprint contract. If reproduction shows it needs the tree-fingerprint binding, stop, record the finding on SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB, and re-scope this item instead of expanding it.
- `--scope changed` runs are keyed per-command through `run_cached()`, so a content edit must change the key; if it does not, the defect is in the changed-scope command/file-list derivation rather than in the fingerprint.

## Related work

- SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (completed) — content-based git-state fingerprint; partial overlap with AC1's original premise.
- SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB (blocked) — tree-fingerprint cache binding for the finish gate.
- SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V (open) — unify the test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout.
- WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (completed) — discovery session.

## OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking)

- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: AC3 keeps today's per-suite `[cached]` marker; is that enough of a signal, or should a cached run also be surfaced at the run/JSON summary level (e.g. `cached_suites`)? Non-blocking — AC3 guards existing behaviour with a test either way.
- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: should the symptom-2 fix also make previously orphaned entries discoverable (re-key on demand), or is preventing orphaned entries (store under a state the operator can reproduce) sufficient? Non-blocking — AC2 only requires that newly stored entries are queryable.
data.title: Test-run cache returns stale results when only the contents of already-modified files change
